areas.summary:
BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md (2,388,244 bytes; 12,047 lines; 176 commits) began on 10-09 as the P3b study "Renewal on runs and the relational reading" (§1–5). Its title and header still describe only P3b, but it grew into the running log of the whole Becoming spine. It has 165 numbered sections, not 162. The layout is: Chinese §1–§162, then one 545 KB "## English summary" block (lines 10227–11960, 176 bold-led paragraphs with no anchors), then §163–§165 with inline English appended after that block. Sections are in landing order, not date order: §83 is dated 10-10 and sits after §82 (10-12); §110 (R5) is dated 10-11; §147–149 (10-15) follow §146 (10-16).

Each section follows one pattern:
- a dateline with Ren's quoted words and a source link;
- a ```text Result(s)/Delta/Supplied premises/Evidence/Boundary/Integration``` block (155 of them);
- a table of declarations;
- the theorem prose;
- an author counterreview (157 of them);
- "readings (AI's, pending Ren)".

The Codex sections §101–109 use a different block format ("Reused:/Record:"). Codex items P89–P105 are not in the log at all; they live in SCIENTIFIC-INQUIRY-CONDITIONS.md, CORE-CONSTRAINT-AND-WISDOM.md and others.

Estimated composition by a heuristic paragraph classifier:
- English summary: 23%
- theorem prose: 23%
- metadata blocks: 18%
- declaration tables: 16%
- counterreviews: 9%
- datelines/provenance: 5%
- boundaries and readings: 5%
- review sections: 17 of them, about 212 KB

The canonical statement of each result already lives in its record (JSON+MD) and in chapter §8/§9. The log is therefore mainly evidence and derivation narrative, not theory that still needs moving into the chapter. The exception is the 141 "待 Ren" and 60 "pending Ren" readings, which are not consolidated anywhere. Some were later decided in place (§152 for P118; §139 by §142) while their headings still say pending.

Structurally, the log's main cost is coupling:
- 565 tracked files mention it, and 34 files carry about 203 anchored links. 105 of those are in the unification plan and 35 in the chapter. All 131 distinct anchors currently resolve.
- There are about 8,075 plain-text "study §N" references, so global § numbers must be kept.
- 158 of 229 records bind the whole file's sha256 as an "integration" source. Every append therefore forces a rebind, and those rebinds have produced 1,598 record-history entries (about 1.8 MB of JSON, mirrored in MD) that say only "section N appended; earlier sections unchanged".
- 24 sections (§125–§161) still say "merge checker receipt pending the integrator's run", while their records bind real receipts.

BECOMING-UNIFICATION-PLAN.md (300 KB, last edited 10-14) is the 10-09 plan. Its phase tables run P0–P88, R1–R6 and P58c, and each row repeats the study section in long form. Tracking moved to _process/BECOMING-WORKBOARD.md on 10-11, but the plan never links the board. Its §10 still says Part II asserts the one axiom (line 313; English line 471), which P128 (study §162, chapter §6.15) reversed. 23 inbound links point at that §10 anchor. The plan's only unfinished row, P36b (sweeping about 2,000 "generative" uses), has no workboard entry.

ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md (54 KB, 10-11 with later partial updates) records Ren's decisions b1–b4 and the re-foundings. Its §4 coordination and §5 continuous-time scope are historical, and its decidability counts (368/226) lag DECIDABILITY-INVENTORY.md (437/263). ZERO-PREMISE-INVENTORY.py is a 52-line candidate-finder that is referenced only by the plan. Its PART2 module set predates P128.

Verified on spot-checks:
- §165's counts (98 theorems and 128 declarations across six P130 modules) match the sources.
- §165's rfl round trip (World.run_world, Run.world_run) matches Runs.lean lines 117 and 133.
- The I5 fresh core run on d21b311a passed: 703 steps, empty core axiom report.

proved.claim: Laws of change with no premise: across any stretch, the end standing plus falls equals the start plus rises; coming to be and ceasing to be are readings of one change across a step (P19)
proved.conditions: None beyond the representation: Nat amounts, discrete steps
proved.assessment: Bookkeeping identities, true by arithmetic on Nat. The prose 'laws with no premise' is accurate only if read as accounting. They are not laws about the world beyond the representation.

proved.claim: In a finite world with decided activity, arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs; without decidability this law is equivalent to excluded middle; asking every finite world for an explicit end step gives LPO; each world-level premise is contingent and independent (P22, P23c, P24, P26, P58)
proved.conditions: Finite relata and decided activity for the iff. The EM and LPO results are constructive calibrations.
proved.assessment: Substantive but modest: a counting argument plus clean constructive-logic calibrations. The study's names follow the R18 and P58c strength corrections ('rests_unrefuted' rather than 'rests').

proved.claim: Transmission through lineage in the additive Price-equation form (P21)
proved.conditions: Finite counts of descent
proved.assessment: An accounting identity, which the log itself says after the P23c correction. The parental term weighted by offspring is not a true selection term. Prose and Lean agree after that correction.

proved.claim: Under the condition Unrestricted, widening is exactly retaining and adding what has significance, keeping is retaining both ways, and mixed is adding both ways. The dynamics leave significance undetermined. The theory states the axiom only as the condition of chapter §6.15 (P39, P56, P128)
proved.conditions: Unrestricted is a hypothesis, never proved
proved.assessment: Under the hypothesis these equivalences are close to definitional. significance_undetermined only shows that significance is a free parameter, as §162 now states. Unrestricted is strictly stronger than G0, per §162 and R18.

proved.claim: The axiom decomposed: along any relation, Unrestricted is exactly the self's presupposition at each standpoint together with one invariance step (P43)
proved.conditions: Stated as equivalences; nothing is derived
proved.assessment: A decomposition, not a derivation; the log says so. The invariance step stays an open philosophical warrant.

proved.claim: For every law of change on finitely many configurations, being lossless (injective) is equivalent to every state returning (R6)
proved.conditions: A finite listing of states (every : ∀ s, s ∈ all)
proved.assessment: The standard pigeonhole fact that an injective self-map of a finite set is a permutation. Correct, but classical; the log's 'zero premise' framing should name the finiteness condition, as the theorem does.

proved.claim: Selection through registration: selections through a registration choose two options alike exactly when the registration identifies them; selection reframed as through a model of the options (P64, I4b-2)
proved.conditions: Option identity decided where options are swapped (written into each Relabel statement)
proved.assessment: Close to definitional: equivariance unfolds to the iff. §151's readings were withdrawn and reframed in §153 with a note kept at the top of §151.

proved.claim: Learning: two histories go alike under induction exactly when the lumping identifies them (P73)
proved.conditions: A lumping (model) given
proved.assessment: Near-definitional characterization. 'Wisdom root formal part' (P75) adds no Lean; it is a mapping in prose.

proved.claim: Identification by bounded records: Moore-type bound N−1 with no decision procedure; tests are N−1 records, exact between two frames; the rest step 2N−1 for every learner; refutation learners rest at a cubic step (P83–P83g)
proved.conditions: States below N; decidable equality where stated (bounded_induction)

Today 156 of the 158 binding records carry a stale sha256 for the log, and the checks pass. Landings after that commit touch 15–23 record files, not about 150. Many of the old history entries also rebind Lean receipts, so they are not 'only appended' notes. My counts: 146 records, 1,593 entries, 1.82 MB, which matches the reviewer's roughly. issues.corrected_fix: Do not split the file to fix churn: the churn is already solved. Splitting would move bytes to new paths, which breaks the path-based reviewed_version lookup (git log -- path) and the existing `path#anchor` citations, and it would force a one-time rebind of 158 records. areas.summary:
This is the Lean periphery that grew before the Becoming spine existed (7–9 October), plus the instance modules that later connected it to the spine. It holds 11,848 tracked files (207.3 MB tracked). There is no lakefile. The root modules and generative-capacity/ use Lean 4.29.1, Std only (lean-toolchain). The Mathlib modules use 4.30.0-rc2 against an external Mathlib project, pinned in lean/periphery-mathlib-pin. Six modules import Mathlib directly: ConnectionistRecovery, CorrectionBoundary, CorrectionHandoff, CorrectionRace, CorrectionRelations and ObservationRepair. Others reach it through imports.

There are 143 live Lean modules (35,146 lines, about 2,530 theorem declarations), plus one failed draft. No axiom, sorry, native_decide or unsafe appears in them.
- The root has 41 modules: the formation, copying and assembly chain, plus WholeGroundCoverage and CutCoverageAudit.
- generative-capacity/ has 89: G0/C/J-conditional comparison, correction and control protocols, judgment, selectors, instances.
- evolution-connectionism/ has 9 modules about connectionist learning, using Mathlib.

How the modules are live:
1. 29 modules are compiled and audited by the core checker each run as inherited modules, because Becoming.Bridge, Becoming.Instances and Becoming.RepairComparison import 19 of them.
2. 11 instance modules import Becoming.* and have their own checkers. Examples are CorrectionInquiry, LearningCorrespondence, MachineInstances and CopyingInstances.
3. 24 records take a module here as canonical_source. 94 records cite the area, and their proof_bindings name 86 sources or receipts, including 11 run-folder receipts.
4. The core checker imports generative-capacity/check.py (check_becoming.py:61), the old FormativeCapacity checker, as its shared audit helper.

The I4a table classifies 137 rows for this area: 31 joined, 57 application, 20 working artifacts, 24 snapshot-only, 3 join candidates and 2 earlier versions. The two earlier versions are SituatedContinuation and SituatedRenewal; both have I4c header notes.

What the spine lacks and only this area has:
- The explicit G0/C/D/J inference audits and rival separations. Examples: EvaluatorGrounding, ProtectionPriorityRival, RelationalGrounding, ClassificationRobustJudgment.
- Correction under observation (CorrectionBoundary and CorrectionInquiry).
- Selector review coverage.
- Gluing of whole comparisons from local charts (WholePracticalRestriction).
- Real-analysis connectionist results (ConnectionistRecovery and LearningCorrespondence).
- Many constructed finite models: protocols, copying machines, assembly and evolution.

Condition. The proofs are sound as far as the receipts go. The organisation is poor:
- **Frozen copies:** 93.1% of files (11,028) and 92% of bytes sit in 345 timestamped run folders. correction-inquiry-checks alone holds 7,652 files (115 runs, 127.8 MB); its 95 runs before 12 October each copied the whole core. 271 runs (9,608 files, 156.7 MB) are not named by any current receipt or record binding.
- **Duplicate snapshots:** another 191 files sit in 21 verification/sources snapshots. All 92 source copies there are byte-identical to the live files.
- **Navigation:** the READMEs are dated status logs from before the spine, and they index 7 of 41 and 15 of 89 modules. The catalogue files all 144 modules under 'ethics', which misleads.
- **Namespaces:** periphery modules declare in namespace Becoming. Because of that, the classification table cites CorrectionInquiry's declarations as spine declarations.
- **Stale periphery receipts:** 10 of the 11 instance modules last passed against core bytes that have since changed.
- **Unverified module:** StructuralInheritance (27 theorems) has no receipt.

The restructure should move the unreferenced run folders under lean/history, keeping their names and adding an index. It should regenerate the indexes and READMEs, split the catalogue group and move the shared helper out of the app folder. Moving or renaming live modules touches about 932 referencing files and needs Ren's decision.

proved.claim: Correction under observation is inquiry. Over supplied admitted histories, an observation map and a success relation: a policy implements correction exactly when its action on each observation value is a common response of the judgment process on that value's cell. A common action exists exactly when every cell has one. A choice is safe at a value exactly when it is a common response on the worlds that show it. The refinement theorems of CorrectionBoundary and ObservationChange follow from the core's commonResponse_antitone.
proved.conditions: Lean 4.30.0-rc2 with Mathlib ea11ccc0, because the imported modules use Mathlib. The step from a common action on every cell to one policy uses choice (selector_iff_common_action). Correspondence to any actual system and the warrant of the success relation are not checked. Receipt correction-inquiry-verification.json (passed 20261015T164111) was built on a core closure in which 67 of 113 modules have since changed.
proved.assessment: Genuine but short. The declarations are the core's common-response law with cells read as beliefs. Their own axiom reports are empty. The chapter text (THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:525) marks this correctly as a periphery bridge. Because the declarations sit in namespace Becoming, they look like core declarations, and MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md lines 678 and 738 cite them under 'Spine'.

proved.claim: Connectionist development as instances of the core laws of learning. A network's development under fixed weights is the orbit of its step. Updating routes make no difference exactly where the update law agrees.
proved.conditions: Mathlib real analysis (tanh). The receipt (learning-correspondence-verification.json, 20261013T095759) used core bytes since changed in 27 of 43 closure modules.
proved.assessment: updating_network_law_iff is a one-line application of adaptive_state_law_iff, a definitional instance. The substantive analysis is in ConnectionistRecovery (29 theorems: one-step Hebbian direction, finite recurrent sensitivity, a sufficient tanh sign-preservation condition). Records generalization-through-lumping and wisdom-root-part-one cite it fairly as an instance.

proved.claim: Seed–edge coverage and a constructive cut audit. Least closure gives exact target coverage. Compatible local grounds glue across scopes. Local domain coverage alone is insufficient. The unrestricted cut-to-coverage upgrade is equivalent to double-negation elimination.
proved.conditions: Std only. verification.json (20261007T110659): 39 theorems, 61 audited declarations, empty axiom dependencies, hashes match current bytes. Also compiled in every core run as inherited modules (Bridge imports both). Seeds and edges are supplied warranted relations.
proved.assessment: Elementary closure algebra; the DNE equivalence is a real, small fact about constructive strength. Becoming.Bridge shows Reached and Reach are reachability on the edge process (record becoming-spine-instances). The README's title 'checked warrant' overstates this: warrant is supplied, not checked.

proved.claim: G0-conditional inference audits. Under explicit G0, a generative extension has a newly positive-relevant claim. Generative extension is a strict order. Continual improvement has no survivor. Under G0 plus a positioned articulation D, every position with access to a response has a reason for it, and independence from endorsement comes from D, not from G0.
proved.conditions: G0, C, P, N and D are hypotheses. After P128 the theory does not assert G0; Part II is conditional. Both modules are in the core run through Becoming.Bridge, which proves the core's definitions equal these by definition.
proved.assessment: Mostly premise unfolding: new_realization_has_positive_relevance is a two-line destructuring. Their value is making each commitment explicit and separable. Records positioned-positive-reason and positive-ground-open-futures state the conditions honestly ('Under explicit G0 …').

proved.claim: From a standpoint's own good to reachable G0. S0, plus unrestricted monotonicity across self and other, plus tolerance and a chain condition, gives G0 on the inventory reachable from that standpoint. An indexed rival that admits only 'mine' is strictly inconsistent once its own generation differentiates such others. A closed self blocks reach.
proved.conditions: S0, supervenience, tolerance and a chain to an own living generation are supplied. The result is standpoint-relative, single-history and limited to the reachable stock.
proved.assessment: A moderate, honest result. Record self-good-reachable-g0 says that the unindexed G0 still needs a bridge from standpoint-relative to normative significance, and that tolerance carries everything beyond S0.

proved.claim: Basic-condition priority is not derivable from no-loss comparison. G0, C and J2 hold together in one constructed protection-versus-gains situation. A trading order also satisfies C. No natural-number score satisfying C represents J2. A bounded rational score does.
proved.conditions: One constructed finite situation; G0 and C are explicit premises
proved.assessment: A genuine, small separation result (proved with omega). It separates J2 from unit-step aggregation only, as its record says.

proved.claim: Joint-bundle information is needed for comparison. Retaining and releasing a coupling have identical marginals, so no irreflexive comparator over marginal-determined summaries implements C. Separately, the comparison under every classification of fresh contents holds exactly when A retains B's fresh contents and is better with all of them treated as secondary; two extreme classifications suffice.
proved.conditions: RelationalGrounding is one event-law construction. ClassificationRobustJudgment is general but uses classical logic. Becoming.CoursesBridge restates it on frames (excluded middle named as a hypothesis; extension case without it).
proved.assessment: Substantive within scope. Both modules are in the core run through the Bridge, and records relational-generative-comparison and classification-robust-generative-comparison match.

proved.claim: A finite review cannot certify every future menu. Coverage on all menus is equivalent to pairwise reflection of the old defeats. For every finite prefix there is a next plan that defeats the compressed output.
proved.conditions: The first theorem holds over arbitrary types with an irreflexive new relation. The failing next plan is a constructed family.
proved.assessment: A general law the spine does not state; I4a classifies it as a join candidate. It has a passed receipt (selector-review-coverage-verification.json). No record cites it.

proved.claim: Local strict comparisons that agree on overlapping charts need not glue into a strict whole order. A joined relation descends exactly when the charts are compatible. A locally strict, compatible three-cycle has no strict extension.
proved.conditions: Std; arbitrary charts. The counterexample is finite.
proved.assessment: A general law not on the spine (I4a join candidate, nearest Becoming.Contextual.glues_iff_agree). No record cites it and nothing imports it.

proved.claim: The parity law of correction relations. A cycle of equal/differ relations has a joint assignment exactly when the number of differ relations is even, and an odd cycle has none. Matching converters restore every root.
proved.conditions: Mathlib leaf, 4.30.0-rc2
proved.assessment: The spine now states the general law: Becoming.Gluing's met_iff_even names cycle_compatible_iff_even as its case (Gluing.lean:59, :838). So this is now an earlier version, although MODULE-CLASSIFICATION still lists it as a join candidate. Its converter and probe theorems remain periphery-only.

proved.claim: Correction and shutdown protocols as instances of the counting and keeping laws. Coverage and safety are kept along every admitted history exactly when each admitted step keeps them. Pending recovery is counted work. Shutdown supervision is a reserved exit.
proved.conditions: Constructed finite protocols. The receipt (20261014T141016) is on core bytes in which Becoming.Return has since changed (docstrings only).
proved.assessment: Instances of general core laws applied to constructed protocols, honestly described in chapter §9. The four records recoverable-mediated-change, mediated-evidence-transport, reserved-shutdown-during-recovery and fallible-witness-diagnosability are scoped to the constructions.

proved.claim: Copying, assembly and acquisition machines as instances. Four copy machines instantiate the copying laws: lineage, doubling rounds k·2ⁿ and the support 9·k(2ⁿ−1). Acquisition, scene binding, goal revision and joint practice instantiate Segmentation, CrossSituational, Gated and Countdown.
proved.conditions: Constructed machines with standard axioms and their own checkers. MachineInstances' receipt (20261014T092451) predates changes in 28 of its 69 closure modules.
proved.assessment: Applications. The general content is in the core laws, and these show the constructed machines satisfy them. They bind 12 records (F10/F03).

proved.claim: Arbitrarily large finite formations across separate histories do not give continued formation along one history. In a four-event tree-building model, every finite depth is reached in some history. Any infinite history that never commissions open only gathers. Under a constant feed, one explicit infinite history builds at every time 2n+3.
proved.conditions: One supplied recipe and feed; toy accounting units; Std with propext and Quot.sound (verification.json)
proved.assessment: A clear, honest constructed distinction. The spine's Run/Stock/Onward laws now state the general form. No record takes it as canonical.

proved.claim: Constructed evolutionary and developmental models: exact cycle and cost criteria, paid finite assembly histories, contact sampling projecting to assembly, Hebbian memory recall, drift margins and calibrated updating.
proved.conditions: The fixed local laws, recipes, schedules and apparatus are supplied. There is no fixation, population convergence or empirical calibration.
proved.assessment: Applications (I4a). The READMEs state their limits honestly. Most are leaves: 51 live modules here are neither imported, record-cited nor in the core run.

proved.claim: StructuralInheritance: two-token templating attachment with cleavage and perturbation (27 theorems)
proved.conditions: No checker exists, and no receipt anywhere binds its bytes
proved.assessment: Unverified. It appears in the declaration catalogue (ethics.md:1727) and in the I4a totals (27 theorems, 'header read') alongside checked modules.

areas.summary:
This area is the pre-spine Lean development: the 32 .lean files at the root of experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/, seven periphery packages, the Lean files outside that tree (1,158 tracked, of which about 161 are live modules) and the I4a classification table.

The core does use the three foundation files, but they sit in three different places. check_becoming.py:65 sets FOUNDATION = GenerativeCore, InquirySufficiency, RelationalRenewal. The receipt becoming-verification.json (20261016T124157.989030Z, passed, core_compiles_from_prelude true) resolves them to GenerativeCore.lean at the lean root, inquiry-root/sufficiency/InquirySufficiency.lean and deeper/RelationalRenewal.lean, and all three hashes match. The imports are at Becoming/Frame.lean:1, Inquiry.lean:2, Keeping.lean:2 and Renewal.lean:2. The checker finds them by file name across the whole lean tree, skips folders that match an exclusion pattern, and asserts exactly one match per name. A restructure must therefore pick history-folder names that pattern covers. Only GenerativeCore and systems-complexity/SystemsOrganization (inherited through deeper/RelationalReduction) from this area reach the spine run.

Condition:
- **Mathematical content:** sound, and the package READMEs scope their claims carefully.
- **Navigation:** stale. The lean/README.md is a 6 October changelog that never links to becoming/.
- **Receipts:** the I4c header notes (bf842fced, 16 Oct, labelled "docs only" on the board) changed only comments, but they broke the byte pins of the "current" default build. Root check.py:160 now fails for 4 modules. Eight modules here have no receipt for their current bytes, and the 5 September draft ExistenceConditions.lean no longer matches its own preserved verification hash.
- **Unrecorded results:** the strongest results here have no canonical record. These include the axiom-free renewal–closure iff (219 empty audits), the naturalism countermodels, controller revision, symbolic chaos and the Lyapunov feedback intervals. `research.py find` returns no record for any of them.
- **File count:** 96% of tracked lean-tree files (49,259 of 51,163) sit in snapshot, run or history folders. In this area, 23 of 35 run folders (255 files) are referenced by no receipt.

MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md (602 rows) is a sound reading table:
- All 432 Becoming.* names it cites resolve.
- No row path is missing.
- In the 25-row sample, no category was wrong. The nuances found: "same" applies to the headline theorem only, one relation is labelled "instance" where it is an analogy, one join candidate is trivial, and import-only entries are filed as applications.

It is not a safe move list:
- Its own rubric says an earlier version "stays".
- 20 of the 31 earlier versions are imported by live modules.
- 58–121 receipts pin their bytes, and about 800 line-anchored links point into them.
- Rows are per file name over 1,580 paths, and 54 names cover more than one distinct file.

Use it to retire earlier versions from navigation; relocate the superseded run folders instead.

areas.summary:
development/ holds 1,274 tracked files (32 MB) in 197 top-level entries, with no index or README of its own. It mixes two eras that share nothing.

(1) The 10-06 to 10-09 pre-Becoming working set: 126 entries, 411 files, 19.8 MB. It has 81 loose snapshot files at the top level (UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING-BEFORE-*.md ×22, UNIVERSAL-ETHICAL-MINIMUM-BEFORE-*, *-BEFORE.json manifests), nine 10-08 "-before" folders, failed or development Lean attempts with logs (connected-model, completion-applicability, continuing-dependency, nondual-applicability), review runs bound by root-foundation *-CHECKS.json (timed-feedback, tuning-correspondence, measured-feedback and others), evidence-extraction folders and one-shot scripts. These bytes are unique: the canonical files were committed only from 10-07, so the snapshots cannot be rebuilt from git. Every recorded preservation hash I checked matches (28 BEFORE manifests and 31 folder manifests). Four chapters and about 75 root-foundation documents link here.

(2) The Becoming landing era, 10-11 to 10-16. There are 50 spent landing kits: 44 becoming-pNN-landing folders, R5 entropy, I3c–I4c and the shared becoming-landing-kit, together 534 files and 7.0 MB. Every module they carry is in the spine. 40 of the 48 Lean copies are byte-identical to the spine blob at their landing commit (git log --find-object); the other 8 are byte-identical to a later spine version. Their study drafts appear verbatim in BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md. Most are linked only once, from the board; 9 are linked from nothing.

Three kinds of material inside this era are not spent:
- **Live tooling in landing folders.** rebind_batch.py and merge_records.py in becoming-general-laws-plan/integration were used for every landing up to P130 today (notes-batch37). Its README calls them "not shared infrastructure (no tests)". integration-i3e/make_checker.py generates periphery checkers. integration-i4a/table.py generates the live MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md, and SPINE-INTEGRATION.py copies its path rules, giving a third rule set beside lean_catalogue.path_role.
- **Record-bound evidence.** 12 records hash-bind 7 files here (framing evidence, p69 Shape.lean, the p72q README, the p77 inventory, p88 provenance and TASK, the P130 report). 85 records link the readability migration tables from their history, and research-check validates those links.
- **Infrastructure reports.** I5 fresh checker run, P129, P130, the Claude takeover audit.

Condition: honest at the scientific level. Kits label AI readings, keep counterexamples and say what is not proved. The problems are structural:
- stale status headers on landed work (PLAN.md and OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN.md say "nothing here has landed", p72q says "Not landed", p86/p87/p88 say "not a completed landing");
- no landed-commit index;
- live tools without tests;
- about 10 new files per landing from re-implementing one workflow (23 apply_docs.py, 12 repoint.py, …).

The area connects to the rest of the repo through the board (54 links), the study (25), records (12 hashed references, 85 history links), 4 chapters, the generated Lean and source catalogues, and frozen JSON or sources files whose bytes must not change.

Restructure plan: generate an index first. Then promote the live tools to tools/research. Then move the spent kits and the 10-06 working set into a history tree with an old→new manifest, following the 2026-10-09 rename precedent (rename-2026-10-09.json and check_rename.py). Keep record-bound files addressable. Moving the Lean files changes the I4a table, for which Ren chose "Nothing is marked or moved until you decide", so it needs Ren's explicit go.

issues.title: Live generators kept in landing folders, and three divergent path-classification rule sets
issues.description: integration-i4a/table.py generates the live root-foundation/MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md. SPINE-INTEGRATION.py copies i4a's COPY and SNAP regexes by hand. tools/research/lean_catalogue.path_role uses a third, different rule: `/history/` and `evidence` count as copies for SPINE-INTEGRATION but not for path_role, and every `_process/` path is 'development-attempt' for path_role. integration-i3e/make_checker.py, byte-identical to the i3d copy, is the generator I4b uses for periphery checkers. A restructure that moves folders changes the three classifications differently.
issues.evidence: MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md L3 says it is generated by development/integration-i4a/table.py. SPINE-INTEGRATION.py L38–40 vs integration-i4a/inventory.py L10 and connect.py L9 vs tools/research/lean_catalogue.py L150–172. `shasum integration-i3d/make_checker.py integration-i3e/make_checker.py` gives c207a417 for both. integration-i4b/README.md L37 runs ../integration-i3e/make_checker.py.
issues.fix: Move the I4a pipeline and make_checker.py into tools/research. Keep a single path-role function imported by lean_catalogue, SPINE-INTEGRATION.py and table.py, and add tests.
issues.verify_reason: The facts hold. SPINE-INTEGRATION.py L38-40 copies the COPY regex from i4a/inventory.py L10 and the SNAP regex from connect.py L9 by hand. tools/research/lean_catalogue.path_role (L150-172) differs from both: it treats every _process/ path as development-attempt, and it does not count 'evidence' or '/history/' as a copy. It says that exclusion is deliberate: 'an arbitrary directory named "evidence" is not necessarily a snapshot'. The i3d and i3e copies of make_checker.py are byte-identical (c207a417), and integration-i4b/README.md L37 runs the i3e copy. MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md L3 names i4a/table.py as its generator. The finding goes too far in presenting all the divergence as accidental. The rule sets serve different measures, and a single function would wrongly merge lean_catalogue's narrow evidence exception with I4a's broad copy rule.
issues.corrected_fix: Move a shared path-classification module into tools/research. It should hold a common base for sources, runs, checks, timestamps and the history segment, with explicit, documented overrides for each measure: catalogue role versus I4a and SPINE copy detection. Add tests that pin the current outputs on today's ls-files, so a folder move shows its effect on all three measures before it lands. Keep the i4a scripts at their path as the generator of record, or regenerate MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md and update its 'Generated by' line in the same change.

issues.title: Landed work labelled 'nothing here has landed' / 'Not landed' / 'not a completed landing'
issues.description: Several headers state a status that is now false, and some of the files are cited by records or the study, so readers following provenance land on stale status. PLAN.md and OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN.md (both L3) say 'Status: proposal awaiting Ren; nothing here has landed', although the plan was executed and OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN L5 itself says PLAN landed. becoming-p72q-quantum/README.md L6 says 'Not landed', although Becoming.Quantum is in the core closure; that README is hash-bound by record contextual-registration. becoming-p86/p87/p88-landing/README.md L3 say 'an evidence draft, not an accepted result or a completed landing', although P86–P88 landed at 9442f66c; the p88 provenance is bound by 2 records and the p86/p87 READMEs are cited in study §§107–109.
issues.evidence: `grep -n 'nothing here has landed' becoming-general-laws-plan/*.md` gives L3 in both files. `git log -1 --format=%s 9442f66c9` reads 'Land feeding closure, relational persistence and finite normal forms (P86–P88)'. `git log -1 --format=%s 6ef63a95e` reads 'Land relational description and contextual registration (P70–P72, P72q)'. The I5 fresh-run summary core_closure includes Becoming.Quantum. contextual-registration.json references p72q README sha 1e9d56073a24.
issues.fix: Leave the original sentences alone. Add a dated status line ('Landed <commit>, study §N, 16 Oct status') or carry the status in the generated index (development-4). For the record-bound README, rebind contextual-registration after the edit.
issues.verify_reason: PLAN.md L3 and OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN.md L3 do read 'Status: proposal awaiting Ren; nothing here has landed', dated 14 October. OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN L5 then says PLAN landed through 26705afc, so that file contradicts itself. becoming-p72q-quantum/README.md L6 reads 'Not landed' (written 12 Oct). P72q landed in 6ef63a95 on 2026-10-13, and record contextual-registration binds that README (provenance role, sha 1e9d5607). The p86/p87/p88 claim is weaker. Their sentence describes the preservation act ('No canonical record ... is changed by this preservation') and the folder's role as a preserved draft, which is still true of the folder. Those READMEs were also added in the landing commit 9442f66c itself. They are dated provenance statements, not false status claims, and the misleading part is the '-landing' folder name. Every one of these headers is dated, so the severity is minor.
issues.corrected_fix: Do not edit the hash-bound p72q README. Record its landed status in the generated development index (development-4). For the unbound PLAN.md and OPEN-ISSUES-PLAN.md, a dated status line appended below the original header is acceptable. The p86-p88 READMEs can stay unchanged, with the index carrying their landing commit 9442f66c.

issues.title: 197 entries and 1,274 files with no index; spent kits do not record their landing
issues.description: development/ has no README, index or manifest. More than 40 kit READMEs never state their landing commit or study section. Nine kits (P49, P53, P55, P58/P59, P58b, P62, P76+P81, P77–P85, P106) are referenced from nowhere outside themselves, and the rest are linked once each from the 276 KB board. A reader cannot tell spent, live and record-bound material apart.
issues.evidence: `ls development | wc -l` gives 197 with no README.md or INDEX.md. The reference census (git grep -o 'development/…' over the repo) gives 0 outside references for becoming-p49/p53/p55/p58-p59/p58b/p62/p76-p81/p77-p85/p106-landing. The 'landed' mention count in kit READMEs is 0 for p76, p77, p78, p79, p81, p82, p83, p84, p85, p86, p87, p88, p106, p107, p109, p110, p116, p117, p119, p121, p124, p125 and others.
issues.fix: Generate a development/INDEX.md and MANIFEST.json from git and the board. For each entry list its class (spent landing, live tool, record-bound evidence, report, review probe, snapshot, attempt), P-item, landing commit, study §, board row and the records that bind it. Give the file an overwrite guard.
issues.verify_reason: Holds, with small count drift. development/ now has 195 entries (concurrent change) and 1,276 files, with no README or INDEX. Eight of the nine named kits have zero references outside themselves. p58b is cited only by the p58c-landing kit inside development/. The landing READMEs I sampled (p76, p77, p78, p86, p106, p125) contain no 'landed' mention. The board is 276,352 bytes.
issues.corrected_fix: As proposed. Generate the index from git, the board and the record references[] scan, so it also lists which records bind each file, and put an overwrite guard on it. Build it before any move, so the move plan can use it.

issues.title: Spent landing kits duplicate the landed Lean and study text (534 files, 7.0 MB)
issues.description: The 50 spent kits carry 48 copies of spine modules (2.6 MB). 40 are byte-identical to the blob at their landing commit and 8 to a later spine version. Their study drafts appear verbatim in the study. lean-index.json lists all 138 Lean files here as 'development-attempt', including the copies of landed modules. The kits are provenance only, yet they dominate the area.
issues.evidence: `git log --format=%h --find-object=$(git hash-object …/becoming-p64-p68-landing/lean/Becoming/Selection.lean) -- experiments/…/Becoming/Selection.lean` gives bca9695b. The same holds for p69 (da8f75a7), p70-p72 (6ef63a95), p76/p81 (8b486cfa), p77/p78/p79/p82/p84/p85 (cfee6329), p86/p87/p88 (9442f66c) and entropy (5cf28c74). A Python line match finds 33/33 lines of becoming-p127-landing/study.md in BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md, and 77/80 for docs/study/p64_zh.md. lean-index.json statistics: 138 dev paths with role development-attempt.
issues.fix: Move the spent kits to a history tree with a manifest (see restructure). Classify kit Lean copies as saved copies in the shared path-role rule so catalogues stop listing them as attempts. Keep the bytes.
issues.verify_reason: Holds with minor count differences. The development tree holds 48 Lean files under */lean/Becoming/, about 2.6 MB. The p64-p68 Selection.lean blob first appears in spine history at bca9695b, and also at f7fffe76. There are 46 becoming-*-landing folders, holding 507 files and 7.7 MB. The finding's '50 kits, 534 files, 7.0 MB' presumably adds other kit-like folders such as p72q-quantum, so the figures are approximate but of the right order. lean-index.json gives all 138 Lean files under root-foundation/development/ the role development-attempt. All 44 non-empty lines of becoming-p127-landing/study.md appear verbatim in BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md.
issues.corrected_fix: As proposed, with a caveat. Some kits hold files bound by records (p77-landing/inventory/INVENTORY.md, p88-landing/provenance.json and evidence/TASK.md). Those moves must go through the development-7 scripted rewrite. Change the path-role classification only through the shared, tested rule (development-2) and regenerate lean-index.json, keeping the 'saved-copy' role for files byte-identical to a landed spine blob.

issues.title: Each landing re-implements the same workflow, adding about 10 files
issues.description: Every P-item kit carries its own apply_docs, make_records, repoint, update_records and apply_inventory scripts. About 800 files were added here between 10-12 and 10-16. This is the process-level form of the 'rebuilding the wheels' Ren warned about on 11 October, and it is the main source of the file growth Ren wants cleaned up.
issues.evidence: `find development -name '*.py' -exec basename {} \; | sort | uniq -c` gives apply_docs.py 23, make_records.py 14, repoint.py 12, update_records.py 11, make_record.py 11, apply_study.py 9, apply_inventory.py 9, config.py 8, record_delta.py 7. Files added per day (`git log --diff-filter=A --format=@%ad --name-only -- development`): 10-12 245, 10-13 122, 10-14 150, 10-15 85, 10-16 197.
issues.fix: Build one tested tool (tools/research/landing.py) that reads a small JSON spec: study section, chapter edits, records from spec, inventory, rebinding. A future kit is then the spec, a README and its receipts list. Record the change in RESULT-WORKFLOW.md.
issues.verify_reason: The numbers hold. There are 23 apply_docs.py, 14 make_records.py, 12 repoint.py, 11 update_records.py and 11 make_record.py, among others. Files added under development/ per day: 10-12 245, 10-13 122, 10-14 150, 10-15 85, 10-16 197, which is 799 in all. A spec-driven landing tool is a real cleanup win. The finding overreaches in calling this Ren's 'rebuilding the wheels'. Ren's 11 October words (sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-11-one-unified-theory-together.md) are about sessions proving separately, not about landing scripts. Applying them to tooling widens Ren's subject, which the project's writing discipline warns against. Also, each script asserts the exact text it replaces, so the kits are a record of exactly what was edited. That evidential role should be kept.
issues.corrected_fix: Build tools/research/landing.py as a tested, spec-driven tool that keeps the assert-before-replace safety and writes a receipt of the edits it applied, so a future kit is a spec plus that receipt. Leave existing kits unchanged as evidence. Describe the motive as reducing per-landing tooling, not as Ren's 'rebuilding the wheels' remark.

issues.title: Canonical records hash-bind evidence inside the scratch-named development folder
issues.description: 12 records bind 7 files here through references[].path with sha256, and one record takes a counterexample source from a kit inventory. 85 records link the readability migration tables from their history, rendered as Markdown links that research.py check_links validates. A move or rename breaks research-check unless the record paths are rewritten. The folder name 'development' also undersells what is canonical evidence.
issues.evidence: A Python scan of records/*.json gives 15 references[].path entries and 1 counterexamples[].path entry into development/, among them worlds-are-runs → p130-frontier-on-base/REPORT.md (6d9aae48), normal-forms-need-decided-apartness → becoming-p88-landing/provenance.json and evidence/TASK.md, process-and-frame-as-readings → becoming-p69-shape-evidence/Shape.lean, and listing-once-is-decided-identity counterexample → becoming-p77-landing/inventory/INVENTORY.md. 85 history[].en/zh entries carry links, e.g. wisdom-root.md L252. tools/research/research.py L172–190 (check_links over rendered record pages).
issues.fix: Either keep these files at their paths, or move them in one scripted change that rewrites record paths and history links by rule. The sha256 values stay unchanged. Verify with a check script modelled on _process/architecture/check_rename.py and rename-2026-10-09.json, then run make research-check.
issues.verify_reason: The core holds. 12 records bind files in development/ through 15 references[].path entries with sha256. There is also 1 counterexamples[].path entry, in listing-once-is-decided-identity, pointing to becoming-p77-landing/inventory/INVENTORY.md. The history entries of 85 records mention development/ paths. research.py check_links (L172-190) resolves rendered Markdown links. The count is off: the bindings cover 8 distinct files, not 7 (framing-evidence/README.md, framing-evidence/Saying.lean, p69-shape-evidence/Shape.lean, p77 INVENTORY.md, p88 provenance.json, p88 evidence/TASK.md, p72q README.md, p130-frontier-on-base/REPORT.md). This is a constraint on any restructure rather than a defect. The remark that the folder name 'undersells' its contents is opinion.
issues.corrected_fix: As proposed: one scripted move that rewrites references[].path, counterexamples[].path and history link paths by rule, with sha256 unchanged, then regenerates the record .md pages and lean-index.json. Verify against a rename table in the style of _process/architecture/check_rename.py, then run make research-check. Do not refresh any hash. The simpler option is to keep the 8 bound files where they are and move only the unbound material around them.

The UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING-BEFORE-WHOLE-PROCESS.md blob (581c0115) is absent from the canonical chapter's history. Check that none of the 135 root-foundation referrers is itself hash-bound before rewriting it. areas.summary:
This area is everything in experiments/ except the integrated-correction tree, which holds the Becoming spine. It has 4,872 tracked files (6.9% of the repo's 70,495) in 22 directories plus experiments/README.md. Almost all of it dates from 4–7 October 2026, before the spine began (about 9 October). Since then the only edits have been mass renames, untracking .pyc files, and the I4c header notes. The exceptions are market-generativity (22 commits, through 15 Oct) and valuation-development.

The material falls into five groups:
(1) Formal Lean lines.
- market-generativity: 28 modules, 874 theorems. Of these, 12 modules (306 theorems) are 'joined' instances of the spine. It is the only experiment cited by result records (10), and the only one besides integrated-correction cited by THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md (§9 peripheral instances).

areas.summary:
These three folders hold most of the pre-spine Lean research from 5 to 9 October 2026, plus its frozen verification. Prefix L = experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean. Tracked files: deeper 2,700 (16.5 MB), inquiry-root 2,954 (61.2 MB, of which inquiry-root/sufficiency is 783 files and 47.3 MB), connected 357 (3.2 MB). Only 167 of these 6,011 files are live Lean modules: deeper 95, inquiry-root 26, sufficiency 46. Another 105 are bespoke check*.py scripts (about 13.5k lines of Python in total), and about 111 are top-level receipts. The rest are frozen run folders (deeper 155 runs with 2,481 files; inquiry-root 76 runs with 2,778 files) and connected/, which is all snapshots, logs and receipts of 6-October builds of lean-root modules.

How these folders relate to the spine: 47 of the 167 modules are compiled in the Becoming spine run (core receipt 20261016T124157.989030Z, 215 modules). Two of them belong to the pure core's FOUNDATION: deeper/RelationalRenewal.lean and inquiry-root/sufficiency/InquirySufficiency.lean (check_becoming.py:65). The other 45 are "inherited", holding 730 theorems in total, many with propext, Quot.sound or Classical.choice. The bridges import 18 of them directly (Bridge, CompositionBridge, JoiningBridge, GranularityBridge, Instances, RenewalBridge) and restate their results with empty axiom reports, as *_by_core or with excluded middle / stable tests named as hypotheses. The remaining 27 are only transitive dependencies; for 8 of these (173 theorems) no bridge declaration references their namespaces. The 120 modules outside the run are classified (as AI readings) in MODULE-CLASSIFICATION.md:
- 12 joined
- 11 earlier versions
- 13 join candidates
- 70 applications
- 14 working artifacts

52 of the 229 records reference these folders, and 22 run folders are proof-bound by records.

What is proved here: Hennessy–Milner-style bisimulation results, joining, composition, granularity and resumption laws, return and trace equivalence, renewal classification, and a premise-tracked derivation calculus (soundness). There are also learning/binding machines and a fallible-inquiry counting bound. One substantive combinatorial result exists only here: the arbitrary-period inquiry lower bound (PeriodGeneralProof, 796 new audits, all empty). It has no record. Elementary join-candidate lemmas the spine lacks are listed under proved.

Condition: the proofs are sound and receipted, but navigation and housekeeping are poor.
- The READMEs are dated changelogs that leave 88 of the 167 modules unmentioned and never point to the spine.
- 4,544 files are byte-identical copies within these folders.
- 130 run folders (2,706 files) are referenced by nothing durable.
- The connected/ checkers would now fail against the live sources.
- 10 modules whose headers the I4c commit edited have no receipt for their current bytes.

Critical restructure constraint: 23 inherited spine modules are bound only by receipts inside deeper/*-checks/<run>/. The core checker's passed_receipts scans LEAN_ROOT.rglob('*.json'), so history moves must stay under the Lean root, or fresh consolidated receipts must be issued first.

areas.summary:
This slice holds 960 of the study's 2,208 tracked top-level files, about 35.7 MB. By type: 399 .md (10.6 MB), 167 *-EDITS.json edit receipts (19.4 MB), 210 *-CHECKS.json receipts (3.3 MB), 153 .py, 28 other JSON, and one .lean, .png and .svg.

Almost all of it is from before the Becoming spine: 934 of the 960 files were last changed on or before 2026-10-09. The files form about 68 multi-note "packets", one per topic, plus 192 single notes. A packet usually holds an -ARGUMENT/-SOURCES/-REVIEW/-MATH/-PROTOCOL/-INTEGRATION.md, then a -CHECK.py, a -CHECKS.json and an -INDEX-EDITS.json. These were companions to roughly 70 older chapters of the generative-foundation programme (G0/J ethics and 慧根, evaluative learning, explanatory necessity, evolution and cognition). The canonical chapter now treats those chapters as records of their original scope (THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:26).

Inbound references, measured by filename over theories/, the workboard, GOALS, tools and config:
- 60 files are cited by records, the canonical chapter, the board, tools or goals.
- 278 are cited only by older chapters.
- 72 only by the generativity chain.
- 246 only by generated catalogues (source-index, lean-index, ARGUMENTS-*).
- 235 only from inside the study.
- 67 nowhere.

The live core is small:
- 19 Becoming independent-review files (P7 to R18, plus the release-readiness review).
- CONTINUATION-GROUNDING-PLAN/REVIEW, DECIDABILITY-INVENTORY.{md,py,lean} and DELEGATED-CHOICES.md.
- GENERATIVITY-CHAIN-INDEX-RECORD.md, the maintenance workflow AGENTS.md names.
- CORE-CONSTRAINT-AND-WISDOM.md and ETHICAL-LEARNING-INTEGRATION.md.
- About 25 record-cited studies from 8–9 October.
- Five build_*.py compatibility wrappers.

The proofs themselves live in experiments/…/lean. No Lean source in the core cites a file in this slice, so moving these files needs no Lean byte change.

Condition:
- Content is generally carefully scoped. The packets disclose hand arguments, supplied premises and AI authorship.
- Navigation fails. The generated README indexes nothing in the folder. 552 of these files count as "working sources" in default `make research-find`, including 147 point-in-time checkers that can no longer pass. Six of those checkers overwrite their own receipt with {"status":"checking"} before they assert anything.
- The 314 KB chain maintenance record buries its workflow under 161 KB of change notes added at the top.
- Review ordinals collide.
- A README-featured result ("connected conditional foundation") rests on a 6 October acceptance by collaborating AI agents. The README calls it "independent".

Restructuring is feasible but is blocked by flat-path assumptions:
- The chain's discovery glob is root-foundation/*.md.
- registry.reviewed_version uses `git log --no-renames`.
- 137 scripts hard-code parents[3] or parents[4].
- Tools hard-code paths.
- About 4,600 path mentions in records and catalogues carry sha256 pins.

A move manifest plus hash carry, as in _process/architecture/rename-2026-10-09.json and check_rename.py, handles these. A folder named exactly `history` is excluded from default discovery with no tool change.

issues.title: README-featured 'connected conditional foundation' rests on AI-internal self-acceptance but is presented as independently reviewed
issues.description: One of the four README-featured results (record conditional-foundation-assessment) has its canonical source in FIXED-FINISH-LINE-AUDIT.md §15 (6 October). Its acceptance in FOUNDATION-ROOT-ACCEPTANCE.md was done by three sub-agents of the same AI session. The source says these are 'collaborating-AI internal reviews, not external peer review'. The README overview says 'independent reviews of the underlying results', START-HERE.md:7 says 'independently reviewed', and the record's does_not_show omits the AI-internal nature. The acceptance also predates the Becoming spine and Ren's 10-11 zero-premise redirect, so its five-condition test is no longer the governing standard.
issues.evidence: FOUNDATION-ROOT-ACCEPTANCE.md:37 'These are collaborating-AI internal reviews, not external peer review'; README.md:136 'Existing integrated assessment and independent reviews'; theories/becoming/results/records/conditional-foundation-assessment.json overview.evidence and does_not_show; theories/becoming/chapters/START-HERE.md:7; _process/research-config.json readme_featured_results
issues.fix: In the record, state 'AI-internal (separate agents of the same system), not external review', add that to does_not_show, and note the pre-spine scope. Ask Ren whether it should stay featured.
issues.verify_reason: The core point holds, but two details are off. What holds: the acceptance was three sub-agents of the same AI session. FOUNDATION-ROOT-ACCEPTANCE.md:37 says these are 'collaborating-AI internal reviews, not external peer review'. Yet the README-featured evidence line (README.md:136, generated from the record's overview.evidence) says 'independent reviews', and START-HERE.md:7 says 'independently reviewed five-condition assessment'. Neither README nor START-HERE says anywhere that 'independent' means separate AI agents. The acceptance (6 Oct) also predates the spine and the 10-11 zero-premise redirect. Off detail 1: the record does disclose the AI-internal nature. Its second progress entry reads 'three separate internal AI challenges ... not external peer review'. The finding is right only that does_not_show and overview.evidence omit it, and overview.evidence is the text that reaches README. Off detail 2: the problem is not specific to this record. 'Independent review' means separate-AI-agent review throughout the repo (README.md:112, :120, :128 use the same wording), so the fix belongs in the shared wording convention as well as in this one record.
issues.corrected_fix: In conditional-foundation-assessment.json, change overview.evidence (en and zh) so README shows 'AI-internal reviews (separate agents), not external peer review'. Add a does_not_show entry for that and for the pre-spine scope (accepted 6 Oct, before the Becoming spine and the 10-11 zero-premise standard). Then make research-render. Separately, define once in README/BRIEF what 'independent review' means in this repo (a separate AI agent, not external peer review). START-HERE.md:7 is chapter prose: correct it, or label it historical. Whether the result stays featured is Ren's decision; ask him, do not unfeature it unilaterally.

issues.title: 2,208 flat files with no index; most are pre-spine yet count as working sources in default discovery
issues.description: The study's generated README, which AGENTS calls the generated foundation-study index, links only the global catalogues. It indexes none of the folder's 2,208 tracked top-level files. In this A–H slice: 934 of 960 files were last changed on or before 2026-10-09, and only 60 are cited by records, the canonical chapter, the board, tools or goals. Yet 552 are 'working' sources in default `make research-find`, because working() excludes only paths with a part named history/development/snapshots or ending -checks/-verification/-development. Those 552 include 147 dead checkers and 272 chapter-companion notes.

issues.verify_reason: Most counts check out. The study README is generated and indexes none of the folder's own files. There are 2,208 top-level tracked files (3,499 in total). The A–H slice has 962 files, 934 of them last changed on or before 2026-10-09. 554 of the A–H files are .md/.py, and working() treats all of them as working sources, because 'root-foundation' matches none of the excluded names. One claim is misleading: 'only 60 are cited'. That figure (I get 62) holds only if the results/data catalogues are left out. Those catalogues bind most of these files: generativity-chain.json names 398 A–H files, source-index.json 471, lean-index.json 181, arguments-a-l.json 101, arguments-m-z.json 50 and session-results.json 11. So most of the 'uncited' files are evidence bound by Ren's curated chain and the reading registers, not dead weight. The chain's historical evidence must not be silently refreshed (AGENTS.md:31). Any history/ move therefore depends on rfAH-5 and cannot be a simple relocation.
issues.corrected_fix: First, have tools/research/navigation.py generate a folder index in root-foundation/README.md, grouping packets by topic or claim and the record or chain row that cites them. That fixes navigation without moving anything. Moving to history/ comes only after the rfAH-5 tool changes. The move needs a manifest that carries the generativity-chain reviewed_sources and known_discovery_paths, source-index, lean-index and arguments register paths, and it must not refresh the chain's historical hashes. Alternatively, mark superseded packets non-working through a manifest that working() reads, which moves no files.

issues.title: Flat-path assumptions block any restructure unless tools change first
issues.description:
Any restructure of this folder must first handle these assumptions:
(1) registry.reviewed_version finds a record's reviewed Markdown version with `git log --no-renames HEAD -- path`. A moved file whose pinned hash differs from its current bytes loses that lookup and counts as drift: DELEGATED-CHOICES.md has 2 such pins, BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md 156.
(2) generativity-chain.json discovery_globs is the flat 'root-foundation/*.md', with 319 reviewed_sources and 1,038 known_discovery_paths keyed by flat paths.
(3) Tools hard-code paths: session_map.py:23-29, navigation.py:211 and 273, reading_catalogue.py:5-6 and 175-176.
(4) 137 of 153 .py files here compute ROOT as HERE.parents[3] (126) or __file__ parents[4] (11), and read siblings as HERE/'X'.
(5) arguments-a-l.json and arguments-m-z.json hold 353 source paths with source_sha256; session-results.json holds 30.
(6) 19 experiments/ scripts name root-foundation files, for example inquiry-root/check_core_tree_integration.py.
issues.evidence: tools/research/registry.py:51; theories/becoming/results/data/generativity-chain.json:8403; tools/research/session_map.py:23-29; `grep -c root-foundation/ theories/becoming/results/data/arguments-*.json` (166+187); `git grep -l root-foundation -- 'experiments/*.py' | wc -l` = 19
issues.fix: Before moving anything: make reviewed_version follow a move manifest (old→new path). Change discovery_globs to include the new layout. Turn the tool constants into config. Then move with a manifest plus a checker in the style of _process/architecture/rename-2026-10-09.json and check_rename.py, carrying hashes only for byte-identical or substitution-only files. Run make research-test and research-check.
issues.verify_reason: Every assumption checks out. (1) reviewed_version (registry.py:46-52) runs `git log --no-renames HEAD -- path`. After a move, pinned hashes that differ from the current bytes are no longer found and count as drift. The finding understates the scale: across the whole folder, 159 of 430 record references to root-foundation .md files, spread over 99 files, pin a hash that differs from the current bytes. DELEGATED-CHOICES.md has 2 of 2 and BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md 156 of 158. (2) discovery_globs is flat 'root-foundation/*.md'. The chain has 319 root-foundation reviewed_sources and 1,038 known_discovery_paths. (3) Paths are hard-coded at session_map.py:23-29, navigation.py:211 and :273, and reading_catalogue.py:5-6 and :175-176. (4) In the A–H slice, 137 of 153 .py files use parents[3] (126) or parents[4] (11). (5) arguments-a-l.json has 166 path mentions, arguments-m-z.json 187 and session-results.json 30. (6) 19 experiments/*.py files mention root-foundation. The proposed fix is sound and risk-aware.
issues.corrected_fix: As proposed, plus three additions. First, make reviewed_version read the manifest old path for any moved file, so that pinned historical versions can still be found (git log on the old path). This matters for all 159 mismatched pins, not just two files. Second, never refresh the generativity-chain reviewed_sources hashes as part of a move; rewrite only the paths, through the manifest. Third, leave the frozen checkers' internal HERE/parents[] logic unedited, because they are evidence and are not rerunnable anyway. Then run make research-test, research-render and research-check.

issues.title: 2,208 flat files with no family index; live and evidence files cannot be told apart
issues.description: The study top level holds 2,208 files (1,246 in I–Z) in one directory. The generated README neither lists families nor marks the 63 live files: record-bound files, board and chapter plans, tool data and compatibility entry points. The 1,183 completed-study files sit beside them under similar names (X-ARGUMENT/X-REVIEW/X-CHECKS).
issues.evidence: ls _process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation | wc -l → 2208 files (excluding subdirs). 1,210 of the 1,246 I–Z files were first committed 10-05..10-09 (git log --diff-filter=A --format=%ad per file). README.md is 2.9 KB, generated by tools/research/navigation.py:211.
issues.fix: Keep the 63 live files at the root. Move the remainder into a dated programme folder with topic subfolders (see restructure). Extend navigation.py to emit a family index and a 'live files' section.
issues.verify_reason: The study top level does hold 2,208 files: 1,246 named I–Z, 1,243 of them tracked. 1,219 of those 1,243 were first added on or before 10-09. README.md (2,878 bytes) is the generated view from tools/research/navigation.py:211. It has only the history links and the historical-section anchors: no family index and no live-file list. I did not recount the '63 live files' figure. The proposed move, though, carries more risk than the finding says.
issues.corrected_fix: Step 1, no moves: extend navigation.py so the generated README shows a family index (prefix → files, date, status) and a 'live files' list. Step 2: move files only after a rename map exists and the moves are made safe. The map must rewrite all 12,196 inbound .md links, chain entries (rf-iz-4) and record paths (rf-iz-5). 212 scripts set ROOT = HERE.parents[3], so moving them one level deeper breaks their root. Frozen copies under development/*-before and _process/architecture/history stay byte-identical.

issues.title: Check scripts overwrite point-in-time receipts in place; reruns now fail and would replace 'passed'
issues.description: 114 of 118 I–Z scripts call write_text on their CHECKS.json receipt unconditionally. Many check the state of documents as it was on 10-06..10-09. Example: LIANGZHI-PRACTICAL-CHECK.py lines 46–48 require each ledger insertion to appear exactly once in AGENTS.md, _process/BRIEF.md, RESEARCH.md and the study README. Those texts have since been rewritten, so the count is 0. Running the script (e.g. as part of a cleanup or 'recheck all') would turn a valid historical receipt into a failed one and lose the passing evidence.
issues.evidence: LIANGZHI-PRACTICAL-CHECK.py:13 OUTPUT = HERE / 'LIANGZHI-PRACTICAL-CHECKS.json'; :46–48 check('owned_shared_fragment', p.read_text().count(row['text']) == 1, ...); :84 OUTPUT.write_text(...). LIANGZHI-PRACTICAL-CHECKS.json:2 "status": "passed". Read-only probe: insertion texts count 0; old theories/shengsheng-buxi-generative-existence files missing; 3 owned files have changed hashes. grep -l write_text root-foundation/[I-Z]*.py | wc -l → 114.
issues.fix: Do not rerun these scripts in place. When moving them to evidence/, add a short README stating that they are historical receipts tied to their commit. If any is revived, make it write to a new dated receipt, or require --write.
issues.verify_reason: The hazard is real but overstated. LIANGZHI-PRACTICAL-CHECK.py does write OUTPUT unconditionally at line 84, and a rerun would fail. All 5 insertion texts that still exist count 0. Two insertion targets and LIANGZHI-EVOLUTION.md are gone with the old theories/shengsheng-buxi-generative-existence tree. Four owned .md files (not 3) have changed hashes: ARGUMENT, INTEGRATION, REVIEW, SOURCES. The counts are 115 I–Z scripts, 112 of them with write_text (not 118/114). Nothing loses evidence: the receipts are tracked, so git keeps the passing version. No make target or tools/research module runs these scripts.
issues.corrected_fix: Mark these scripts as historical receipts bound to their commit, for example in a README beside them. If one must be re-run, write to a scratch path or a new dated receipt, never over the tracked receipt. Restore any accidental overwrite from git; never 'fix' it by re-recording hashes.

issues.title: 11.8 MB of edit ledgers duplicate git history
issues.description: 199 edit ledgers (*EDITS, *ADDITIONS, *INDEX-ATTEMPT, *CONCURRENT-NOTES, *CORRECTION .json) store full before/after texts of edited documents, which git already holds. LANGUAGE-AND-FORMATION.patch (1.67 MB) is a diff of NONDUAL-METHOD.md and others. Together they are about 40% of the area's bytes, and they dominate grep and search noise.
issues.evidence: RELIEF-APPRAISAL-EDITS.json = 1,531,069 bytes, of which the 'before' payload is 1,409,657 bytes (11 full prior texts). RELIEF-AND-RECONSIDERATION-EDITS.json 1.40 MB. Total of the 199 ledgers 11.76 MB (du over the glob).
issues.fix: Do not delete. Move them under evidence/. Optionally add a sidecar index mapping each 'before'/'after' payload to its git blob, so readers can use git. Only with Ren's go, consider storing the payload outside the default search path (e.g. a compressed evidence archive kept in-repo with its sha recorded).
issues.verify_reason: The sizes hold. There are 204 matching ledgers (not 199), totalling 11.85 MB, about 38% of the 31.3 MB of I–Z bytes. RELIEF-APPRAISAL-EDITS.json is 1,531,069 bytes, about 1.48 MB of it 'text' payload. The 'duplicates git' premise is false, though. 4 of the 11 'before' texts in RELIEF-APPRAISAL-EDITS.json match no git blob: GENERATIVE-GROUNDING.md, RESEARCH.md, the shengsheng README and sources/SOURCES.md. They preserve uncommitted states that only the ledger holds. Moving the ledgers would not shrink the repository; it would only cut grep noise. That is a minor win.
issues.corrected_fix: Keep all ledgers byte-identical. A sidecar index may map each payload to a git blob where one exists, but it must mark the payloads that have no blob as the only copy. Never replace a payload with a git pointer. Leave relocation or archiving to a later step with Ren's go, and record each file's sha.

issues.title: Registry drift resolution does not follow moves; 46 record-bound files cannot move safely
issues.description: When a referenced Markdown hash differs from the reviewed one, reviewed_version looks up the reviewed blob with git log -m --raw --no-renames HEAD -- path. After a move the old blob sits on the old path and is not found. Tolerated growth then becomes hard drift. This already matters: record laws-of-one-step pins ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md at reviewed sha 4b80bef5…, which differs from the current file. 43 records hold 70 hashed refs into 46 I–Z files.
issues.evidence: tools/research/registry.py:46–80 (reviewed_version). python3 over theories/becoming/results/records/*.json: 46 I–Z files referenced, 70 refs; one mismatch, laws-of-one-step → ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md (other three records citing it match).
issues.fix: Phase 1: do not move record-bound files. Phase 2: teach registry.py to read a rename map (as with _process/architecture/rename-2026-10-09.json) and query the old path. Add a test and run make research-test, then move.
issues.verify_reason: The mechanism is real. registry.py:46–80 runs git log --no-renames on the current path only. The counts are close: 43 records, 71 refs (not 70), 46 files, and exactly one mismatch, laws-of-one-step.json pinning ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md at 4b80bef5. The impact is narrower than stated. A file moved unchanged, with its record path rewritten, still matches its record's sha directly, so no history lookup is needed. Only refs already drifted (1 today) or files edited after the move would lose their reviewed blob. ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md is a live plan that would stay at the root anyway.
issues.corrected_fix: Leave drifted or still-edited record-bound files in place. Move record-bound files only when unchanged, and rewrite the record paths in the same commit. Before later edits to moved files, add rename-map support to reviewed_version (query old and new paths), with a test and make research-test.

issues.title: 16 universal-grounding attempts with no single ledger
issues.description: About 80 files make up 16 separate attempts at universal or no-axiom ethical warrant. Each ends 'not established', but nothing joins them. No page states which premise each attempt lacked, which counterreview defeated it, or that the current position is G0 folded as a condition (Part II as conditional §6.15, P128). A reader meeting any one of them cannot tell it is one of 16 failed or open attempts, or which is latest.
issues.evidence: Conclusions: WHOLE-PROCESS-GROUNDING-INTEGRATION 'not yet established'; WHOLE-PRACTICAL-GROUND 'not complete'; WHOLE-CONTINUATION-WARRANT '未完成'; WHOLE-ETHICAL-IDENTIFICATION 'does not prove'; WHOLE-GENERATIVE-AUTHORITY-COUNTERREVIEW 'remains unestablished'; UNIFIED-GROUNDING / STRONGEST-CLAIM / UNIVERSAL-WARRANT-SUFFICIENCY / RECURSIVE-WARRANT 'does not establish'; NORMATIVE-WARRANT 'does not prove'; NECESSITY-ATTEMPT 'not established'; NONINSTRUMENTAL-ROOT '未完成'; ZERO-AXIOM-PRACTICAL-JUDGMENT 'not established'; YITI-REN-UNIVERSAL-PROOF-ATTEMPT.md:5 '当前结果：…未完成'; ZERO-AXIOM-CLASSIFICATION '尚未完成'; UNIVERSAL-METAETHICS-LEAN-INTEGRATION 'Full universal meta-ethics: not proved'. Record universal-practical-warrant is target/open.
issues.fix: Generate an attempt ledger (one row per attempt: date, target, premise missing, defeating review, superseded by) in the ethics-grounding folder README. Preserve all attempts; this is a failed-candidate record per AGENTS.
issues.verify_reason: All 16 families exist, 68 files rather than about 80, and the quoted 'not established' conclusions hold (e.g. YITI-REN-UNIVERSAL-PROOF-ATTEMPT.md:5). 'Nothing joins them' is false. theories/becoming/chapters/UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING.md (412 KB) is a chronological narrative citing 10 of the 16 families, each with its result. The preserved historical README/RESEARCH copies list 13. Record universal-practical-warrant.md:86 says earlier attempts keep historical scope with no universal completion. What is missing is a compact one-row-per-attempt ledger that names the current position (P128, G0 as condition). That is a navigation improvement, not a major failure.
issues.corrected_fix: Add a compact attempt ledger (date, target, missing premise, defeating review, later scope) in the study's ethics-grounding index. Link each row to its section in UNIFIED-ETHICAL-GROUNDING.md and to record universal-practical-warrant. Leave the attempt files and Ren's source texts unedited, and preserve them all as failed-candidate records.

areas.summary:
This area has 1,921 tracked files (45.5 MB). Across all of sources/ there are 6,373 tracked files and 1.7 GB on disk; most of that size is outside this area (situated-recovery, evolutionary-selection, 20-codex-theory-sessions, 18-friend-conversations). The area holds two different kinds of material.

(1) Imported originals, 00–14 and 15-user-provided. These are byte copies of Ren's earlier lineage, made 2026-09-03 to 10-02: the 2021 Metamunity proposal and Pages files, wamotopia, the meta-attractor drafts, speculative-future, zhishan, 生生不息论 v1–v13 and the SSBX docs, the 間/文 language notes, STS/bonfire/Yi, context-runtime/ember and the museum. They also include derived Markdown renderings: 381 of 719 claude.ai chats, Claude memory files, and prompts extracted from Claude Code sessions. Preservation is strong:
- `git log --diff-filter=MDR` shows no modification, rename or deletion after import. The one exception is the documented 2026-09-25 replacement of the nested wamotopia .git by a bundle.
- All 1,241 file rows in SOURCES.md's original listing match the current byte sizes. The 381 chat files match `_SELECTED-INDEX.tsv` one to one.
- All 12 recorded SHA-256 values I could check match.
- The "non-ASCII variants" that `git ls-files` shows come from git quoting the path (532 quoted paths). No split ASCII/non-ASCII directories exist.
- The real numbering problem is that two directories are numbered 15-.

(2) sources/15-codex-theory-conversations. It holds 262 Markdown records, 1 attachment .txt and 1 attachments folder, dated 09-05 to 10-16. It is the canonical store of Ren's exact directives, and 2,254 files reference it. The separation of Ren's words from AI text is very good: quotes are verbatim (typos such as "agetns.md" kept), and the AI context sits under its own heading. Across the whole git history only one blockquoted line was ever changed, and it was an AI correction note. Of 939 relative links, 938 resolve.

The weakness is navigation, not preservation:
- The directive register links 55 of the 264 entries.
- 35 records appear in no index (register, GOALS, goal JSON, SOURCES or AGENTS). Twelve of them are dated after 10-09, including the 10-14 relation-first refounding ("please, finish all") and the 10-15 note that "the core covers the whole of reality".
- The register mixes chronological orders.
- `make research-find` skips sources/ altogether.
- SOURCES.md, the only sources manifest, stopped on 10-09. It has 43 broken links to the renamed `theories/shengsheng-buxi-generative-existence/unified-2026-10-05/`. It has grown into a 369 KB append log with several insertion zones, and its original header now sits at line 416.
- SOURCES.md labels 14-claude-code-prompts as Ren's own messages. In fact 517 of its 756 blocks (87% of the characters) are harness task notifications.
- 15 AI-authored research write-ups and 2 conversation exports (about 0.4 MB) are stored among the directives.

How it connects: result records, GOALS (generated from _process/goals), the register, the workboard and the chapters all cite directive records. 367 files mention sources/SOURCES.md as provenance.

Overall condition: strong preservation, weak indexing. Recommended restructure:
- Keep every original and the 15- path in place.
- Generate a hash manifest and a directive index.
- Split SOURCES.md into a frozen ledger and a compact current manifest.
- Complete the register.
- Let research-find search directives.

areas.summary:
experiments/integrated-correction holds 1,533 tracked files (about 144 MB) outside lean/. It has three layers that came at different times. (1) 5 October: the financial "integrated correction" specialization. This is the root README, CENTRAL-CLAIM, RESULTS, VERIFICATION, verify_model.py, model/, results/, review/, plus constitutional-extension, governance-closure, viability-control and systems-dynamics (63 files). These are fee, payer and custodian ODE models with hand proofs and numerical audits. (2) 5 October: the general-framework proposal (README, review/) and its studies closure-study, gap-resolution and reproduction-test (142 files). They add finite criteria, hand proofs and public-data reanalyses. (3) Under generative-basis: the 5-Oct study (formal/, checks/, figures/, review/, integration/, MANIFEST, checkplans), then evidence packages from 6–16 Oct. These are mathematical-abstraction (543), noninstrumental-concern (336), ecological-selection (216), inquiry-correspondence (98), biological-scale-correspondence (25), semantic-evidence, situated-kitchen-evidence, necessity-symmetry and renewal-closure. Two unrelated experiments, selective-handoff and endogenous-continuation, are also filed here.

Connection to the canonical theory. Only 7 of 229 records cite anything in this area outside lean/. Four reviewed-scoped empirical records have inquiry-correspondence as canonical_source. Three recorded-checked records (selection-through-a-model-of-the-options, lifting-where-branching-is-finite, what-a-finite-history-refutes) bind periphery instance modules in mathematical-abstraction that join PluralRecords/TieBreaking, FiniteBranching and PrefixSafety to Becoming.Selection, Lasting and Horizon. Layers (1) and (2) have zero records and almost no chapter links; FORMATION-PRIOR-ART cites gap-resolution. They are historical and well scoped, but they still serve as the entry READMEs of the directory that contains the formal spine. None of the four READMEs on the chain (IC, general-framework, generative-basis, lean) links to lean/becoming/README.md.

Condition. Links are healthy. The only broken links are in frozen snapshots, plus one false positive from LaTeX. The focused research check is clean for the 7 records. Problems found:
- The 9 Oct rename rewrote selective-handoff/PROTOCOL.md and two design files that FREEZE.json binds. verify_results.py would now fail.
- The three instance receipts were built with Lean 4.30.0-rc2, although the package lean-toolchain files declare v4.29.1. P129 changed the spine bytes they compiled against.
- The generative-basis, mathematical-abstraction and noninstrumental-concern READMEs are reverse-chronological status logs. One stale line says no new Lean is claimed.
- inquiry-correspondence has no README.
- There are 426 byte-identical copies (17 MB). Snapshot paths reach depth 22 and 349 characters.

Location. The spine's path names three superseded 5-Oct studies. It cannot move alone. The spine run compiles 215 sources from six places under lean/: 137 in becoming/, 39 in deeper/, 29 in universal-ethics/, 8 in inquiry-root/, GenerativeCore.lean, and 1 in systems-complexity/. check_becoming.py also uses LEAN_ROOT=HERE.parent. A move means relocating all of lean/ (51,163 tracked files). 3,009 tracked files contain the path string (90,735 occurrences). Of these, about 1,741 live files need rule-based rewriting, about 240 generated views need regenerating, and about 1,028 evidence files keep their old bytes. 124 of 351 live lean/ scripts resolve the repo root with fixed parents[N]. Cache keys and record-receipt bindings use content hashes, so they survive. The 9-Oct rename machinery (rename manifest, check_rename.py, former-path table) can carry the move, but only at a quiet, merged point and only with Ren's go. Recommended now: index READMEs and pointers. Recommended later: one coordinated lean/ relocation, with the historical layers moved to a history location.
