issues.title: Footnote says the one axiom derives G0 'that living and further generation have basic positive significance'; what is proved is weaker
issues.description: The footnote, also rendered into README.md line 68, and the chapter's one-sentence summary say that with the axiom as a condition the work derives G0 with its full content: living AND further generation, POSITIVE normative significance. What Lean proves is weaker in two ways. First, Unrestricted makes sig true of everything. The derived 'G0' is therefore unvalenced significance of every claim, living or not, and 'positive' is weakened to 'has significance'; chapter line 691 admits this ('weakens “positive” to “has significance”'). Second, the formal `living` readings explicitly contain no further generation (Metaethics.lean docstring lines 9-14: 'Neither contains further generation'; premise card line 141). So the headline description of the proved result is misleading, and 生生's specific positive standing remains a reading (§6.12: 'what is positive is the living, 生生; this reading ... is the AI's').
issues.evidence: OPENING.md:64 '[^axiom] ... the work derives G0 (that living and further generation within the whole have basic positive significance)'; README.md:68; THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:32 ('G0, that living and further generation ... have basic positive normative significance, is a theorem'); THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:691; Significance.lean:388-397 (premises_of_unrestricted: proof is `reads p c (unrestricted ...)`); Metaethics.lean:9-14
issues.fix: Change the AI footnote and one-sentence wording to: 'with the axiom as a condition, every claim, and so every living claim, has significance from every standpoint (G0 with “positive” weakened to “has significance”); that what is positive is 生生 is a reading, and the formal living readings do not contain further generation.' Ask Ren before touching OPENING body text; the footnotes are AI-written.
issues.verify_reason: The core point holds. `Unrestricted` (Significance.lean:131) makes `sig` true of every standpoint, step and formation. `Valuation.premises_of_unrestricted` (Significance.lean:388-397) is a one-line instantiation: `all p c _ := reads p c (unrestricted ...)`. `Valuation.Significant` (Metaethics.lean:168) says only that every living claim has `sig` from every standpoint. So the derived 'G0' is unvalenced significance, and the living content plays no role. The chapter itself says at line 691 that the axiom 'weakens “positive” to “has significance”', and Ren's own axiom text (Significance.lean:11) says 'doesn't have to be positive'. Calling the result 'basic positive significance' in OPENING [^axiom] (line 64), README:68 and chapter line 32 therefore overstates it. The second sub-claim is off. `premises_of_unrestricted` is generic over any `V.living`, including a reading that contains further generation. The 'Neither contains further generation' docstring (Metaethics.lean:9-14) applies only to the readings the Becoming layer supplies, not to the theorem. The real point is that under Unrestricted the reading of living is idle. Severity: the theorem is correct and the weakening is disclosed in §6.8, so this is a misleading headline gloss rather than a wrong result. Major, not critical.

So propose the wording to Ren rather than editing it. issues.title: 'The dynamics do not decide significance' comes from toggling a free parameter, so it shows an omission in the representation

Yet the claim does central work: OPENING (Ren's text plus footnote [^axiom], [^ethics]) argues that the law 'does not show that others count too' and that 'only the axiom rules out' bounded significance. In the method's own terms this is an omission (World contains no significance variable). It is not an explanatory finding about becoming. Ren's own view in Significance.lean lines 13-16, that a center and its boundary form within cognitive dynamics, is exactly the fuller structure that might remove the toggle.

issues.title: Rest, novelty and forgetting laws depend on integral amounts with a fixed unit; prose generalizes them
issues.description: Dissipation is defined as losing at least one unit per uptake (Dissipation.lean:224-231, `total give + sign(total take) ≤ total take`), and levels are Nat. The rest theorems (World.rests_unrefuted etc.) are well-foundedness arguments on Nat, and 'novelty needs gain' / 'a part held within a bound returns and forgets' are pigeonhole on Nat. Record laws-at-finer-units already shows the rest/recurrence laws fail at a refining unit unless refinement is counted as a giving. A continuous closed dissipative system (e.g. exponential relaxation) never stops changing in finite time, and a bounded real-valued system can be new at every step. OPENING line 9 ('whatever is closed cannot go on forever without coming to rest') and chapter line 1269 ('novelty needs gain') do not mark this dependence. 'Natural-number amounts' is disclosed as a representation commitment, but nowhere is it said which headline laws are artifacts of it.

issues.fix: Add a 'representation dependence' column to the premise card and records, recording for each headline law whether it survives replacing Nat by an ordered abelian monoid or by reals, and a refining unit. Qualify OPENING's footnote [^conditions]: 'with amounts in a fixed smallest unit; at refining units the rest laws need the refinement counted as giving (laws-at-finer-units)'. Body text needs Ren.
issues.verify_reason: The Lean facts are right. `DissipatesOn` requires `give + sign(take) ≤ take`, so at least one unit is lost per uptake (Dissipation.lean:224-226). The Novelty laws, including `Web.exceeds_of_new` and `Web.returns_of_bounded`, are pigeonhole arguments on bounded Nat stocks (Novelty.lean header and lines 101, 112). A bounded real-valued system can be new at every step, and exponential relaxation never rests. The claim that 'nowhere is it said' is refuted for the rest laws. Part I stated whole says 'These laws of rest rely on the natural-number unit, in which every exchange loses at least a unit under dissipation' (line 1275, zh line 1177 '这些静止的规律依赖自然数的单位'), with the Emission/Alternation witnesses. OPENING [^law] (line 54) also discloses 'whole-number amounts'. Lines 481, 485 and 489 say 'real amounts are not derived'. Two gaps remain. (a) OPENING [^conditions] (line 56) and Ren's line 9 state the rest law for 'ours' with no unit caveat; [^conditions] reads it from the second law, which supplies no minimal loss quantum. (b) For the bounded-part 'returns/forgets' and 'novelty needs gain' laws (line 1269), the dependence on a discrete bound is not stated next to the claim. Major remains appropriate for the headline physical reading.
issues.corrected_fix: Chapter, both languages: add the unit/discreteness dependence next to the novelty and forgetting laws at line 1269 and its zh counterpart, mirroring line 1275. Records: add a limitation line to the Novelty records ('bounded Nat stock: pigeonhole; a bounded real amount can be new at every step'). Do not add a new premise-card column without the board/integrator. OPENING [^conditions] is Ren-controlled: propose a clause to Ren, 'with amounts in a fixed smallest unit; at a refining unit the rest laws need the refinement counted as giving (laws-at-finer-units)', and do not edit it unilaterally.

issues.title: Premise card says a definite global causal order is 'not assumed', but every World has one global linear step index
issues.description: World's flow and web are all functions of one Nat step index shared by every relatum (Space.lean:177-180; Flow.lean:222-225; Dependence.lean:168-173). Order.lean recovers the partial order of joined exchanges as the invariant under commutation, but only for histories that already have a linearization. Indefinite causal order (the quantum switch, cited in record theory-of-becoming-foundation progress) cannot be represented. The 'not derived' list (line 201) already says 'the shared index of steps' is supplied, so the card's 'Not assumed' entry contradicts the chapter's own §1.

The wording 'at every interface' is inherited from the earlier framework: in record theory-of-becoming-foundation, the quantum-switch counterexample challenges 'definite causal order at every native operational interface'. It can be partly defended, because Becoming.Order shows that only the commutation-invariant order of exchanges registers. So the registered causal order is not assumed to be total, while a definite linearization is. The item misleads only mildly: the representation commitment is stated nearby. Minor, not major.

issues.title: Unity results are encodability results, presented as what the space is
issues.description: Item 1 of the full statement and §1 present World.unity ('every world balances and is one run of the law of exchange'), Contextual.world ('the readings in context of one unfolding are always one world, with no gluing') and Frame.world as substantive unity of readings, read as Ren's 'there are no two realities'. In Lean: World.withRest adds a relatum that takes or gives exactly the truncated imbalance (Imbalance.lean:68-75), so any Nat level sequence is a run of exchange. The unity-of-readings record says 'any level sequence, so any world, runs by exchange'. Contextual.world puts any step-indexed predicate family into World's `active` field with nothing standing or flowing. These show that World is expressive enough to encode the other representations. They do not show that the represented whole is relationally one. There is also a method tension: NONDUAL-METHOD line 13 says conditions 'need not be quantities that can be stored or exchanged', while every condition is a Nat stock and every change is exchange.

So 'every world balances and is one run of exchange' is an encodability result, and the unity-of-readings record statement itself says 'any level sequence, so any world, runs by exchange'. `Contextual.world` puts step-indexed claims into `active` with 'nothing standing or exchanged'. The overclaim charge is weaker than stated, however. Item 1 at line 99 is tagged '[representation, theorems]'. It says the rest is 'counted as a relatum (adopted by Ren the same day)' and that the readings form a world 'with nothing standing or exchanged in it'. It does not claim that these theorems establish 'no two realities'. The non-trivial content, that the world's own readings glue exactly where it balances (`Flow.changeReadings_glue_everywhere_iff`), is stated. The NONDUAL-METHOD:13 tension is minor: Contextual.world represents non-quantity conditions through `active`.

issues.title: 'Zero axiom' through conditional theorems is the deduction theorem; the distinctive content is not stated
issues.description: Part I 'uses no axiom' because every premise appears as a hypothesis, and the G0/Part II folds turned asserted axioms into antecedents. Any axiomatic theory T ⊢ φ can be restated as ⊢ T → φ, so this alone does not distinguish the account from an axiomatic one. Ren's target ('the whole thing ... is deductively necessary', line 42) is the stronger claim. The chapter keeps this apart (line 51/58 and record theory-of-becoming-foundation status open), but the slogans in OPENING ('None of this needs an axiom', Ren's text) and the one-sentence summary ('The theory uses no axiom') do not name the deduction-theorem point. The genuinely distinctive content is: (a) premise-free laws, which are definitional or arithmetic; (b) independence, binding and minimality of premises; (c) constructive equivalences such as law_iff_em. None of these says that the premises are necessary.
issues.evidence: THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:30-32, 51, 58, 173-175, 1133 ('It uses no axiom, ethical or substantive'); OPENING.md:11; theories/becoming/results/records/theory-of-becoming-foundation.json (status open)
issues.fix: Add one sentence to the one-sentence summary and Part I's preamble: 'Stating premises as hypotheses does not by itself remove them (any axiom can be made an antecedent); what Part I adds is that its premise-free laws exclude nothing beyond the representation, that its premises are independent and bind, and where classical principles enter. Whether the premises and the representation are necessary is the open target.'
issues.verify_reason: The logical point is correct: stating every premise as a hypothesis is the deduction theorem, and it does not by itself distinguish the theory from an axiomatic one. The chapter, though, already says that 'an empty Lean axiom report is not an absence of premises' and that 'An absence of ethical axioms is not an absence of substantive premises' (lines 51/58). It keeps the necessity deduction open (line 126, foundation §5; record theory-of-becoming-foundation status open). Line 1133 names part of the distinctive content: the laws 'exclude nothing beyond the representation', and whether premises hold is empirical. So the strong zero-axiom target is not silently narrowed, and the AGENTS.md concern is met. What is missing is an explicit sentence, near the slogans 'The theory uses no axiom' (line 32) and 'uses no axiom, ethical or substantive' (line 175), that conditional form alone is cheap. That is a framing improvement, not a stale or false claim.
issues.corrected_fix: Add the proposed sentence to the chapter's one-sentence summary and the Part I preamble (lines 30/32, 173/175) in both languages. OPENING line 11 is Ren's body text: raise it with Ren rather than editing.

issues.title: Reading balance as conservation and dissipation as the second law conflates energy with exergy
issues.description: Footnote [^conditions] says the work reads balance and dissipation from conservation and the second law. In the model, though, balance plus dissipation on the same Nat level means a closed family's total strictly falls whenever anything is taken: the amount is destroyed in exchange, with no environment relatum. A conserved quantity cannot behave like that. The consistent physical reading is free energy or exergy, which changes only by transfer and by destruction. As written, the correspondence is inaccurate.

open_questions: Does Ren want the headline zero-axiom claim restated with the deduction-theorem caveat? In other words, should 'zero axiom' mean 'no premise asserted', with the necessity of the representation and premises kept as the open target, or should it be reserved for that stronger target?

Which representation should the canonical laws be stated for? Should the premise-free and rest laws be re-proved over an ordered abelian monoid or reals (where rest, novelty-needs-gain and forgetting fail or need refinement counted as giving), or should the opening's 'whatever is closed comes to rest' be explicitly restricted to quantized amounts?

D1 reads 生生 as widening within a pre-given type of formations. Is this compatible with Ren's 8–9 October correction that reading 'generative' as any new admissible organization is a misreading? Under Unrestricted, a part that admits one more formation of any kind without loss counts as generative.

Is there a construction that makes significance a function of World data (e.g. from registration or wanting continuation, Ren's 'a center and its boundary exist only within cognitive structure and dynamics')? If so, Web.significance_undetermined would no longer apply to the fuller structure. This is the result that would most change the account's ethical route.

The record theory-of-becoming-foundation next_delta asks for 'every becoming is representable as the spine represents worlds'. Which concrete classes are the first targets for faithful embedding into World with the premises preserved: continuous-time Markov chains, reaction networks, quantum channels with indefinite causal order? Indefinite causal order looks like a principled counterexample to the shared step index.
Should AGENTS.md line 19 and GOALS.md line 75 ('G0 axiom route authorized') be updated to the folded status? Both are Ren-owned instruction texts.

areas.summary:
OPENING.md (23 KB, 94 lines) is Ren's text, edited with AI. make research-render places it at the top of README.md through readme_opening in _process/research-config.json; the README copy is in sync. Ren's original words are in sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-10-truth-exists-opening.md. These sentences are Ren's: the universal invariants, "basis of all ethics", "explains good and evil", "no absolute self", the alignment and cancer passages and the sages. The specific laws in paragraphs 7, 9 and 11 are AI elaboration. The v6 accuracy edits (04d084ac) already brought the strength of the conclusions in line with Lean: the double-negation rest and feeding results now read as "cannot go on forever without". The footnotes are mostly careful and honest.

The gaps that remain are in the **conditions** and in a few **readings**:
- Paragraph 9 names only balance and dissipation. Each theorem also needs a census, every relatum embodied, finite enclosure, and finite distinct families.
- By the work's own later result (World.withRest_balanced, World.withRest_closed_iff), balance holds by reading: original balance is exactly the rest never active. So "nothing comes from nothing" is closure of the bookkeeping, not a feature of "ours".
- Dissipation as defined is a whole-unit least loss per exchange. That is stronger than the second law. Passing (Entropy.lean:1862) is finite, balanced, lossless and enclosed, and goes on forever. The Resolution witnesses show that rest needs the quantum.
- "Nothing that goes on is closed" is unconditional in the main text.
- "Explains good and evil" leaves mixed parts unordered (Transfer.unordered). It is also relative to a counterfactual that holds the others fixed.
- The derivation of G0 is immediate (G0 is the axiom restricted to living claims). The footnote and "In one sentence" present it as a substantive derivation awaiting review.

In the chapter:
- The English item 11 says the readings of 生/生生 "are Ren's". The Chinese says the AI decided them under delegation D1.
- Item 4 still says the world "comes to rest", where only ¬¬ is proved.
- "C is a law" is an identity by definition.
- "The theory stated in full" is 72 KB. Items 3 and 4 are single paragraphs of 8–12 KB with 50–80 declarations each, which makes the section unreadable as a statement of the theory.
- The premise card, linked from [^conditions], does not list the World premises at all.

issues.title: 'Universal invariants, a law of how anything comes to be' exceeds what the premise-free laws say
issues.description: The universal (premise-free) part is definitional identities, arithmetic identities and counting consequences. The chapter itself says they 'exclude no unfolding beyond what the representation itself excludes' and 'are not dynamical content'. Every dynamical 'how' (rest, feeding, joint excess) is conditional. Worlds with no change satisfy the premises (holding_world, idle_world), so 'becoming happens' in every universe is not a theorem. Note for Ren: the sentence is the thesis; a reader takes it as the proved universal part.
issues.evidence: theories/becoming/chapters/THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:100 (EN item 2); Becoming/Change.lean:542 (Iff.rfl); Becoming/Openness.lean:1129 holding_world; Becoming/Space.lean:535 idle_world
issues.fix: Note for Ren: consider 'a set of universal invariants of change, and laws of how anything comes to be... under the conditions they name', or point [^law] to chapter item 2's 'not dynamical content'.
issues.verify_reason: The core point holds. The premise-free laws are identities and counts: Web.change_readings is six Iff.rfl at Becoming/Change.lean:542, and chapter line 100 says they 'are not dynamical content'. But the sentence is mostly Ren's own thesis. sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-10-truth-exists-opening.md:11 reads 'universal invariations, that for every universe, becoming happens, the law follows'. Only the clause 'a law of how anything comes to be, lasts, changes and passes away' is AI elaboration. On 16 Oct the v6 proposal (drafts/2026-10-10-opening/OPENING-V6-PROPOSAL.md, 'Left as they are, for Ren') deliberately left this sentence to Ren. The next two paragraphs (OPENING.md:7, :9) split what holds 'in every universe, by what change is' from what holds only under conditions, and [^law] (line 54) marks representability and necessity as Open. One cited piece of evidence is wrong. idle_world (Space.lean:535) is not a world without change: its relatum rises ('A relatum rising by what it gives itself') and only Balanced ∧ ¬Acting is shown. holding_world (Openness.lean:1129) is the valid witness that the eight premises allow no arising or ceasing. This is a note for Ren, not a major overclaim. A separate small staleness: the header comment at OPENING.md:1 still says 'version 5 of the drafts', but v6 was applied in 04d084aca.
issues.corrected_fix: Note for Ren only; do not edit without Ren. Offer the AI-added clause as optional wording ('a law of how anything comes to be ... under the conditions it names'), or have [^law] say first that the universal part is identity and counting, not dynamics. Separately, and with Ren's go, update the header comment from 'version 5' to 'version 6'.

World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed also needs a census (finitely many active, listed), every relatum embodied, and every step enclosed from some step on, meaning the exchange lies within finitely many conditions. Flow.fed_from_beyond needs a finite distinct family, Around (finite enclosure), and DecidableEq. joint_excess_ends needs Dependent, Acting and gated renewal at need >= m. World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed (Openness.lean:705-707) requires Counted (a census) and Embodied (every relatum stands exactly while active), as well as balance, dissipation and enclosure from some step on. Embodiment is not idle. Openness.lean:1234 rest_needs_standing gives `throughput`: Counted, ArisingEmbodied, Balanced, Dissipative, enclosed around at every step, with arising recurring. That is a direct countermodel to the main-text sentence 'wherever ... nothing comes from nothing and nothing passes on without loss ... whatever is closed cannot go on forever without coming to rest'. Flow.fed_from_beyond (Continuation.lean:151-153) also needs Distinct, Around from some step on, and DecidableEq. [^conditions] does name the census and embodiment ('with further premises named in each theorem'), so the overclaim sits only in the main text. issues.title: Dissipation as defined is stronger than the second law; 'as in ours' is contested at equilibrium
issues.description: DissipatesOn requires every taking formation in a closed family to lose at least one whole unit per step. That is the source of the rest bound. The second law is statistical and permits reversible, equilibrium exchange with zero net loss. Passing is finite, balanced, lossless and enclosed, with arising and ceasing recurring forever. The Resolution witnesses show that rest fails at refining units without a quantum or a proportion of loss. The Entropy record itself says 'the correspondences to thermodynamics are readings, not physical derivations', and the chapter never mentions the second law. So 'whatever is closed cannot go on forever without coming to rest', read of our universe, holds only at a grain at which every exchange loses (coarse-grained, away from equilibrium).
issues.evidence: Becoming/Dissipation.lean:224-232; Becoming/Entropy.lean:1862-1866 Passing.passes; Becoming/Resolution.lean:1-140 header (Asymptote, Trickle, rest_needs_quantum); theories/becoming/results/records/entropy-history-and-record.md 'Does not show'; grep -i 'second law' chapter = 0 hits
issues.fix: Note for Ren: add to [^conditions] that dissipation is a least loss per exchange (Entropy record law 4), that lossless closed worlds go on (Passing), and that the second-law reading is coarse-grained; consider wording 'nothing passes on without loss' as the condition, not as a description of 'ours'.
issues.verify_reason: The core point holds. Flow.DissipatesOn (Dissipation.lean:224-232) requires give + sign(take) ≤ take. So every taking formation in a closed family loses at least one whole unit at every step, which is stronger than the physical second law, since that law allows reversible exchange with zero entropy production. Entropy.lean:1862 Passing.passes is finite, enclosed, balanced and lossless, with arising and ceasing recurring forever. The entropy record says 'The correspondences to thermodynamics are readings, not physical derivations' (entropy-history-and-record.md:50). The chapter has 0 matches for 'second law|thermodynam|热力学', so the footnote's reading 'from conservation and the second law' has no anchor in the chapter. One detail is off. The Resolution module shows that with the refinement counted, rest holds at every resolution with no premise added (World.rests_unrefuted_refinement_counted, Resolution.lean header lines 20-30). rest_needs_quantum and Asymptote fail only when the refinement is not counted. So 'rest fails at refining units' is not the right statement of the limit. The real issue is the strict per-exchange loss, and that 'as in ours' asserts this of our universe. [^conditions] already calls whether actual unfoldings meet the conditions 'an empirical question', which softens but does not remove the main-text assertion.
issues.corrected_fix: Note for Ren. In [^conditions], say that dissipation here means a least loss at every exchange in a closed family, that lossless closed worlds go on without rest (Passing.passes), and that reading it from the second law is a coarse-grained reading away from equilibrium (link entropy-history-and-record). Do not cite the Resolution witnesses as showing that rest fails at refinement; with the refinement counted, rest holds. Optionally add a sentence to the chapter's premise card so the footnote's thermodynamic reading has an anchor.

issues.title: 'Nothing comes from nothing' as balance is, by the work's own P107 result, a matter of reading

World.withRest_closed_iff shows that original balance holds exactly where the rest is never active, which is closure. The chapter (item 3, end) now says balance, Acting and Taking 'hold by reading', and that what remains are the states of parts: closure, dissipation, embodiment, transmission and decision. issues.title: The derivation of G0 from the axiom is immediate but is presented as a substantive result awaiting review
issues.description: Unrestricted sig means that every standpoint, step and formation is significant. Valuation.premises_of_unrestricted then gives G0 by instantiation. areas.summary:
This area is the coordination and status layer of the Theory of Becoming. Most of it is out of date.

**The work board** (_process/BECOMING-WORKBOARD.md, 276,352 bytes, 374 lines) was set up on 10-11 as the place to claim work and queue landings. Its header says it "records who is doing what, not scientific status". In practice it has become a landing log, with receipts, theorem counts and statements in rows up to 3,151 characters long. 106 of its 118 item rows are closed. Of the other 12:
- Nine are stale. They still read "verified in scratch, handed to the integrator" for items that have landed on main: P118, P119, P120, P123, P124, P125, P126, P127 and P108.
- One is superseded by P128: "Part II … awaits Ren".
- One is the zero-premise inventory, which is committed.
- One is W-root. It is held by a Codex session that has been inactive since 10-13, and its target is still open.

The "Current continuation" section is dated 10-13 and says "not pushed"; in fact origin/main equals main. No row names the current integrator; the last explicit handover is to Codex on 10-13. The queue is empty after P130 and I5.

**GOALS.md** is generated from 15 goal JSONs, and 11 of them have not changed since 10-08/09. The first-priority Becoming goal is current in its premises (P128 fold), but two things are stale:
- Its "Next" field is still the 10-11 zero-premise redirect, which the release review calls executed.
- It links only 9 of the 229 records, all from the 10-10 era. 192 records belong to no goal.

**The umbrella target record**, theory-of-becoming-foundation, is substantively unchanged since P30 (10-10).

**ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN** has every class-(b) decision recorded as decided. Yet its header still says "pending Ren", one status paragraph says the imbalance relatum was "not adopted" (it was adopted 10-14), and its §4/§5 coordination text is obsolete.

**OPEN-QUESTIONS.md** lists only the 4 open targets. The 12 further-proof groups in chapter §8 and Ren's pending decisions are missing from it.

**Chapter §8** is the best current statement of what is open. It has two gaps:
- Its review paragraph stops at the sixteenth review.
- Its "What stays Ren's" list leaves out the readings posted after the delegation, which are pending Ren in the records: P120, P123, P125, P126, P127, and P130's two.

**What remains for Ren's stated end** ("unified, complete, enclosed, zero-axiom"):
- The core is axiom-free and checks fresh: I5 run on d21b311a, 703 steps, empty axiom report.
- Still open:
  - the necessity of the whole (theory-of-becoming-foundation);
  - "enclosed": 12 groups of further proofs in §8;
  - unity: 792 of 7,214 theorems are still apart under the extended base (P130);
  - 39 I4 join candidates in five themes, with 20 more left outside for now.
- The representation commitments that Ren reserved (discrete steps, ℕ amounts, census, decided equality, listing) are themselves premises.
- The step of invariance (the crux of §6.15) is Ren's to state.
- The axiom-free ethical step is not attempted.

**Git.** There are 88 registered worktrees:
- 22 are prunable (their directories are gone);
- 79 HEADs are already ancestors of main;
- 2 have uncommitted changes;
- 4 directories under .claude/worktrees are not registered.

There are 142 local branches; 131 are merged into main. The 11 unmerged ones are 3 patch-equivalent copies, 7 superseded heads kept on purpose, and 1 evidence branch. Nothing needs landing.

areas.summary:
This area is 41 directories. Git tracks about 4,451 files and 1.35 GB here, roughly 70% of the 6,373 tracked files and nearly all the bytes in sources/. They fall into five kinds that the current layout does not tell apart.
(a) Ren's own words. sources/16-claude-code-directions holds 15 verbatim direction records with a clear split between Ren's text and the assistant's gloss. sources/18-friend-conversations holds machine transcripts (ASR) of three recordings and Ren's clarifications.
(b) Documents Ren supplied whose authorship is AI or unverified: 17, 19 (the GPT review package for IASEAI v5), collective-alignment.
(c) AI session evidence: 20 (a raw snapshot of seven Codex workspaces, 2,402 files and 341 MB), 22 and 25 (supplements from the repository reconciliation), and 21 and 23 (Ren's verbatim request plus an AI completion narrative).
(d) Snapshots of Ren's earlier code: 26.
(e) Third-party literature and datasets: 24, 27–42 and every named directory. The largest are situated-recovery (423 MB of Dryad MAT files in plain git), evolutionary-selection (348 MB, mostly byte-range fragments of BioImage Archive microscopy), 28-agentdojo (39 MB) and 32-mental-state (36 MB).

Byte provenance is excellent. I recomputed SHA-256 for every hash record I could resolve: 7,794 matched and none genuinely failed. The 111 differences in 22 and 25 are by design. Those manifests pin capture-time git blobs, and all 1,546 pinned blobs exist. Labelling of Ren's words against AI text and ASR output is careful throughout, as are licence notes for many datasets and boundaries on what each reading covered.

The weaknesses are in navigation and structure:
- The theory-directory rename (87fdbb077, 2026-10-09) touched no file under sources/. That left 43 broken links in sources/SOURCES.md and 14 more in non-frozen READMEs in this area.
- SOURCES.md is a 369 KB file built in layers. Its first 423 lines are 211 status paragraphs added at the top, its totals are stale (1,811 files), and it omits developmental-attention and market-generativity entirely.
- Ren's directions are split by tool and folder. 16 stops at 10-04, while 52 later Claude Code directions sit in 15-codex-theory-conversations. The directive register links 16, 21, 23 and 25 zero times.
- Ren's own recordings (213 MB of audio) exist only on the local disk. Meanwhile, about 413 MB of third-party data that can be downloaded again is committed as ordinary git blobs.
- Number collisions (32 and 36 each appear twice), mixed naming schemes, missing group READMEs (20, evolutionary-selection and others) and subfolders their parent README never links (13 of 14 in 37) make the area hard to read.
- 30 of 60 PDFs have no licence wording nearby. Full transcripts of a conversation with a named friend are committed with no consent note.

Restructuring must respect how much depends on these paths. Experiment receipts and checkers cite them about 67,000 times in JSON (63,368 for 28-agentdojo alone) and in about 150 code files. So the plan should leave external-data directories where they are and reorganize them through a registry and a regenerated index. Only the AI session snapshots, the directive and status records, and small attachments are worth moving physically, with a path map. Moving files does not shrink the 5.8 GB .git, because the blobs stay in history.

areas.summary:
This area is everything around the Theory of Becoming. There are 1,589 tracked files (about 296 MB), and about 1.6 GB more sits on disk ignored.

The 16 branch folders under theories/ hold 61 files (55 MB). They are AI-written syntheses of the sources/ corpus from 2026-09-03, built on one template ("theory in one paragraph", Claims, Genealogy, "In Ren's own words"). Fourteen of them have had no substantive edit since 2026-10-04. Their only later change was the 10-09 slug rewrite, which introduced some drift in meaning. Their citations into sources/ resolve well; I found 0 missing in most folders. They are honest about what they rest on.

Only theories/meta-attractor is live. Its 10-08/10-13 pages tie the neutral meta-attractor definition into the Becoming core (ContinuingRevision, ReferencePlan, Revision) and into periphery Lean packages with receipts. A Lean-checked ledger rejects parts of the 2025 formal layer, but those claims still stand uncorrected in the README body.

Navigation is the main weakness:
- The branch folders are reached only through MAP.md, which is frozen at 2026-10-04 and still describes theories/becoming as the old 生生不息论 folder.
- The current generated index, theories/becoming/results/THEORY-MAP.md, is not linked from README.
- AGENTS.md and the generated location tables never mention drafts/, output/, tmp/, worldbuilding/ or work/.

drafts/ has 15 dated folders (1,339 tracked files, 52 MB). 1,113 of those files are one paper line, IASEAI v1–v7.3. Its folder root still presents v2, and whether it was submitted is not recorded. The 1.4 GB on disk is almost entirely ignored film renders (1.35 GB), which were never committed.

Publishing work is scattered across three folders: sources in drafts/, builders in tmp/pdfs, exports in output/. Guardian Anarchy is spread over four places: drafts, an experiments gitlink, output images and a tmp tarball. Its copies reached origin/main even though the project's README records a local-only instruction. The transcription pipelines behind Ren's spoken "why and meaning" sources exist only in ignored tmp/.

worldbuilding/ is a healthy self-contained subproject: it has its own AGENTS.md and its validator passes. It accounts for 159 MB of tracked binaries, including a fully redundant 15.6 MB zip.

Nothing here is a wrong Lean claim. The proofs in this area are of three kinds:
- Lean periphery or core instances (meta-attractor).

areas.summary:
tools/research/ holds the shared research infrastructure: 9 modules (2,855 lines) and 7 test files (1,146 lines). __pycache__ exists on disk but is gitignored, not tracked. research.py is the CLI: check, render, find, imports, lint, snapshot and preserve-view. registry.py validates the 229 canonical records (schema 1 and 2), receipt bindings and scoped Markdown drift, and renders the record pages and RESULT-REGISTER.md. navigation.py renders the 11 overview pages, with overwrite guards and history preservation. style.py is the readability lint. Four older generators are not part of `make research-check`: reading_catalogue.py, lean_catalogue.py, generative_chain.py and session_map.py. Paths come partly from _process/research-config.json and partly from hard-coded constants. _process/architecture/ holds the manifests, the preserved history (113 files, 12 MB) and the 10-09 rename receipt.

Condition. `make research-test` passes (101 tests, 73 s). `research.py check` passes in about 16 s: 0 errors, 0 drift. All 213 recorded-checked records are bound to passing receipts by source hash, and 97% of their declared names are confirmed against the declaration lists Lean produced. The core guard machinery works: render lock, input snapshot, per-output overwrite guard, and preservation of the exact bytes plus a link-adapted copy.

Problems:
- **Overclaims.**
  - 3 records cite the shared boundary "no Lean axiom is used", but their bound declarations depend on Classical.choice and propext. The tools do not enforce the boundary's own cite_when rule.
  - The README sentence "It uses no Lean axiom" is hard-coded in navigation.py. It is wider than the chapter's precise claim about the core.
- **Checks give no signal.** CI has not run since 10-15 because of a GitHub billing failure. Even running, its shallow checkout would turn all 248 changed_outside_cited pairs into drift.
- **Search misses the main study.** `make research-find` skips files over 2 MB, which includes the main live study BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md.
- **Stale generated views.** Four families sit outside the check and are linked from every page: the reading catalogue, the Lean catalogue, the generativity chain and the session map. All four are stale.
- **Bloat.** The 261 generated tracked files total 30 MB.
  - Record pages are 11 MB, largely rendered history. 5,365 of 7,564 history notes (4.8 MB) only record a rebind with the claim unchanged.
  - The same 229-row table appears on 4 pages, and GOALS.md and ROADMAP.md have the same content.
  - DEPENDENCIES.md is 555 KB.
  - lean-index.json is 8.6 MB and was committed 90 times since 10-09.

What changed_outside_cited 248 means: 248 (record, source) pairs, 158 records, 4 files. 156 pairs are only insertions into the append-only study. 89 are lines rewritten elsewhere in the canonical chapter. This is the intended behaviour and I found no false pass. The guarantee is narrower than it looks, though: only the lines that link the record are protected, `###` anchors give no protection, and insertions never count. It is also a hazard for restructuring: moving any of those 4 files turns its pairs into drift.

What a restructure needs that does not exist yet:
- a general move command with a receipt (the 10-09 rename generator was never committed, and check_rename.py is tied to one receipt);
- reviewed-version lookup that follows moves;
- one shared evidence classifier (there are three, and they disagree);
- a link check across live documents;
- config-driven paths (three config keys are declared but unused);
- the landing kit promoted out of development/ into tools/research. There are 316 per-landing scripts, which shows the gap.

78 external check scripts import the tool internals, so their API must stay stable or those scripts must be frozen.

issues.title: Three records cite 'no Lean axiom' while their cited declarations use classical axioms
issues.description: Three records cite the standard boundary no-ethical-premise, rendered on their pages as 'No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used': every-origin-passes-the-gate, lifting-where-branching-is-finite and what-a-finite-history-refutes. Their bound periphery receipts list propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice for declarations the records cite. This breaks the boundary's own cite_when rule ('bound receipts report an empty axiom list for every cited declaration'), which registry.validate never checks.
issues.evidence: standard-boundaries.json:9 (cite_when). Records: every-origin-passes-the-gate.json:96, lifting-where-branching-is-finite.json:145, what-a-finite-history-refutes.json:127. Axiom dependencies: receipt becoming-checks/20261015T182331.625376Z gives Becoming.LivingOrganizationCorrespondence.presence_reflected -> [propext, Quot.sound]; PrefixSafetyCorrespondence.holds_of_prefixClosure_by_core -> [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] (receipt 20261015T184605.889457Z). Rendered at records/every-origin-passes-the-gate.md:30.
issues.fix: Remove no-ethical-premise from the 3 records, or add a core-only key such as 'core-declarations-axiom-free'. In registry.validate, implement cite_when: for each record citing the key, look up receipts' modules[].axiom_dependencies for every declaration on its proof sources, and fail on any that are nonempty.
issues.verify_reason: The claim holds exactly as stated. 80 records cite no-ethical-premise. I scanned every one, checking the declarations each names against the axiom_dependencies in its bound receipts. Exactly these 3 cite declarations with non-empty axiom lists. The boundary's cite_when ('empty axiom list for every cited declaration') is never enforced: registry.py only checks that the keys exist and are not repeated (lines 332-335). Each page also contradicts itself. Its evidence line says the periphery instance is checked 'with standard axioms', while its boundary line says 'no Lean axiom is used'.
issues.corrected_fix: Do not change the shared boundary text. Edits there re-render all 80 citing pages and need record-level review. In the 3 records, replace the key with a new one, e.g. 'no-ethical-premise-core-axiom-free': 'No ethical premise; the core declarations use no Lean axiom; the periphery instance uses Lean's standard axioms.' Do this with a record review and history note. Then implement cite_when in registry.validate. Look up each cited declaration in the bound receipts' modules[].axiom_dependencies, and fail when one is non-empty.

issues.title: README's scientific framing is hard-coded in Python and overstates 'uses no Lean axiom'
issues.description: The README paragraph saying the theory 'uses no Lean axiom: each law is proved under the conditions it names', together with the G0 framing, is a string literal in navigation.py. It has been edited there 5 times (P4, rename, P36b, opening, P129). README_MARKER (line 25) tells editors to edit records, config and the opening file, not navigation.py, so the text is outside record review. The chapter's precise claim is narrower: the core's source declarations have empty axiom reports; the generated injEq lemmas depend on propext; the periphery uses standard axioms.
issues.evidence: navigation.py:220 and :25. README.md:102. Chapter theories/becoming/chapters/THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:1524. git log --format=%s -- tools/research/navigation.py
issues.fix: Move the paragraph (and the bilingual blurbs at navigation.py:243-252) into a Markdown file named in research-config.json, beside readme_opening, and name that file in README_MARKER. Scope the sentence to the core, e.g. 'Its core uses no Lean axiom; periphery instances use Lean's standard axioms where stated.'
issues.verify_reason: Two parts hold. The paragraph is a string literal at navigation.py:220. README_MARKER (line 25) does not tell editors that this text lives in navigation.py. The overclaim is weaker than stated. As an account of the theory, meaning the core, the claim is accurate. The chapter (line 1524) says every source declaration has an empty axiom report, and the only axiom-dependent constants are generated injEq lemmas that no source declaration uses. The periphery is outside the core by the chapter's own definition. A scoping clause would make the text more precise; it is not a wrong claim. The text was also reviewed in a commit (25560d2d1, P129 release review), not left unreviewed. The edit count is off: 8 commits touch the file, though not all touch this paragraph.
issues.corrected_fix: Move the paragraph to a configured Markdown file next to readme_opening, e.g. theories/becoming/README-FRAMING.md, and name it in README_MARKER. The text is AI-authored, not Ren's opening, so it may be edited. Still, put the scoping change ('Its core uses no Lean axiom; periphery instances use Lean's standard axioms where stated') through the same review as the P129 wording.

issues.title: CI gives no signal: billing failure, and a shallow checkout would break scoped drift
issues.description: No CI run has started since 2026-10-15T16:38Z: 'recent account payments have failed'. The last run that executed failed at the research-check step after tests passed. actions/checkout@v4 defaults to fetch-depth 1, and registry.reviewed_version needs the reviewed blob in HEAD's history. In a shallow clone, every changed_outside_cited pair (248 today) becomes '(reviewed version not in history)' drift, exit 2.
issues.evidence: gh run view 38907343839 (annotation: job not started, billing). gh run view 38770654741 (check step failed). registry.py:51 (git log on HEAD). Reproduced in a scratch shallow clone: scoped_drift -> ['(reviewed version not in history)'].
issues.fix: Add 'with: fetch-depth: 0' to the checkout step. Ren must resolve GitHub billing. Optionally fall back to the 'settled' hash when history is unavailable, and report it as a warning.
issues.verify_reason: Every recent run fails. The latest (38907343839) never started: the annotation says recent account payments have failed. The earlier run 38770654741 passed the test step and failed at the check step. The workflow uses actions/checkout@v4 with no fetch-depth, so the clone is shallow. In code, reviewed_version runs 'git log ... HEAD -- path'. In a depth-1 clone that finds only the tip blob, so changed_lines returns None. scoped_drift then returns ['(reviewed version not in history)'], and check exits 2 for every one of the 248 changed_outside_cited pairs. I confirmed the logic from the code but did not repeat the shallow-clone run. The blob-hash cache in ~/.cache also does not exist on a CI runner.
issues.corrected_fix: Add 'with: fetch-depth: 0' to the checkout step. Ren must resolve the billing problem. Do not fall back silently to the current hash as a substitute for review; the fallback should only emit a warning, never pass silently.

issues.title: changed_outside_cited protects only the record's link lines; ### anchors and insertions never count
issues.description: For a Markdown source, the reviewed part is (a) the lines that link the record's page and (b) the `##` sections cited by anchor. sections() only recognizes '## ' (line 91), so a record citing a level-3 anchor gets no protection for rewrites in that subsection. Insertions are excluded (line 113), so a retraction appended inside a cited section passes. Both were demonstrated in a scratch repo. Of the 248 pairs, 89 are role 'statement' on the canonical chapter, where §6, §8 and §9 were rewritten since review (49 records still reviewed at chapter version 787bfafbcb). The check reports only a bare count, not which files or records.
issues.evidence: registry.py:86-94, 108-114, 141-147. Scratch demo: rewrite inside a cited '### 1.1' section gives None; insertion inside a cited '##' section gives None. research.py:235 reports only len(GROWN).
issues.fix: Report the 4 files and per-file record counts. Section at every heading level that a record cites. Optionally count insertions inside cited sections. After review, add a 'settle' command that rebinds pairs with no cited change, with one ledger note.
issues.verify_reason: The mechanics hold. sections() matches only r'##\s', so a '###' line falls under its parent '##' heading, and a cited level-3 anchor never intersects the parent's anchors. Insertions are excluded (op in replace/delete). I confirm 248 pairs: 156 on BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md, 89 on the canonical chapter, 2 on DELEGATED-CHOICES.md and 1 on ZERO-PREMISE-PLAN.md. 49 chapter pairs remain at reviewed sha 787bfafbcb. Only the count is reported. The impact is smaller than implied, though. Only 2 records (4 citations) cite level-3 anchors: constitutive-binding-assessment and universal-practical-warrant. Excluding insertions is the documented design ('lines only added change nothing reviewed', registry.py:97-101, 133-134), not an accidental gap. A record's own linked line in the chapter still counts when rewritten. The 'statement' role label is not in GROWN, which has no role field.
issues.corrected_fix: Report per-file and per-record counts. Section at the heading levels records actually cite. Do not add an automatic 'settle' command. AGENTS.md forbids refreshing a source hash merely to silence a failure. Any rebind must follow an actual reading of the changed sections, recorded with the reader's note, e.g. a 'research.py settle --reviewed <ids>' requiring an explicit list.

areas.summary:
This area covers the physical health of /Users/ren/theories rather than its theory content. HEAD tracks 70,495 paths holding 3.40 GB, but only 21,188 distinct blobs (2.79 GB). The file count is dominated by evidence. 50,191 files (71.2%) sit in 885 timestamped run folders, mostly Lean checker receipts with frozen copies of sources and logs under experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/. becoming-checks alone has 31,786 files but only 3,014 unique blobs. 12,647 tracked files are empty, nearly all zero-byte .log files. Canonical material (theories/, the 229 records, tools/, root files) comes to about 735 files, roughly 1%. The 229 records cite only 754 distinct paths, which bind 98 of the 885 runs. Bytes are a different story: in the object store, cost is dominated by imported binary datasets (.mat 418 MB, .pdf 205 MB, .bin 165 MB, .png 147 MB, .npz 111 MB, .zip 103 MB, packed). The run folders cost only about 16 MB packed, because their text deltas compress well, but about 670 MB and 48k files in every checkout. Tracked-file growth was 3,889 (10-05) → 41,518 (10-10) → 70,495 (10-16).

.git is 5.8 GB:
- packs 3.91 GB in 34 packs; pack-ff337… (1.82 GB, 53,644 objects) is wholly contained in pack-cb20b… (1.85 GB);
- 344 MB of tmp_obj_* garbage from interrupted writes (Oct 6–13);
- 177 MB of loose objects (5,285) and 177 MB in LFS (one object);
- 1.2 GB of per-worktree admin indexes (87 entries, 22 of them prunable because their directories are gone).

The unique object set is about 2.5 GB on disk. 28,008 objects (0.45 GB) are unreachable from any ref, reflog, worktree HEAD or index. The local refs/codex/* refs alone hold another 0.38 GB, including a non-LFS 185 MB .mat blob. gc.pruneExpire=never is set, but reflog and worktree expiry are not, and auto-gc keeps warning about unreachable loose objects. The GitHub copy is private and 1.44 GB.

Disk is the most urgent problem. 69 live worktree checkouts at about 3.6 GB each take about 228 GB on a volume that is 91% full (82 GiB free). Every one is merged or patch-equivalent. Two hold unlanded checker runs, and one of those runs, 20261011T170859.998618Z, is cited on main but exists only untracked in .claude/worktrees/jolly-pike-140c94.

CI has given no protection since 2026-10-15 16:38Z. It went red when scoped-drift landed: the depth-1 checkout cannot supply the reviewed versions that 248 record bindings need. Since 18:37Z jobs have not started at all, because of GitHub billing.

Other findings:
- experiments/guardian-anarchy is a gitlink with no .gitmodules and no remote.
- The root .gitignore has 3 lines.
- tmp/ and output/ are tracked.
- 789 paths exceed 260 bytes.

Recommended direction, nothing executed:
1. Preserve the unlanded runs, then retire the clean merged worktrees, and use sparse checkouts for agents.
2. Consolidate .git with cruft-pack gc under never-expire settings, with no prune and no history rewrite. 298 receipts cite source_commit and 293 commit SHAs are cited in Markdown, so LFS migration of history is ruled out.
3. Thin the run folders: keep every JSON receipt and every referenced file in place, and retire the other ~49k files into per-run manifests (path, size, sha256, blob id, anchor commit) recoverable from history.
4. Fix CI with fetch-depth 0 and filter blob:none.
5. Send future large datasets to a separate evidence store with manifests.

issues.title: CI has been red since scoped-drift landed and has not run since 10-15 18:37Z
issues.description: actions/checkout@v4 runs at its default depth of 1. registry.reviewed_version finds a reviewed Markdown version by running `git log HEAD -- path`. In a shallow clone only the HEAD blob is visible, so scoped_drift returns '(reviewed version not in history)' for each of the 248 drifting bindings, and the check exits with code 2. The last green run (1a6c7c41, 16:32Z) does not contain the scoped-drift commit f6816a74. The first failure (108e278e, 16:38Z) does, and 18 runs in a row then failed in the 'Check records…' step. Since 18:37Z, 39 runs never started because of a GitHub billing block. main currently has no automated guard. The CI log text was not retrievable; the mechanism is confirmed from the code and the current data.
issues.evidence: gh run list -L 300: 18 failures with steps=6 starting at 2026-10-15T16:38:11Z (run 38770654741, failing step 'Check records, evidence bindings…'), then 39 with steps=0 and the annotation 'recent account payments have failed'. `git merge-base --is-ancestor f6816a74e 108e278e5` succeeds; it fails for 1a6c7c414. tools/research/registry.py:51 (git log HEAD -- path), :138-139, :814 (return 2 if scoped_drift). A Python scan finds 248 record sha256 bindings ≠ current bytes, all .md.
issues.fix: Restore billing (Ren's decision). In research.yml set `with: fetch-depth: 0, filter: blob:none`; optionally add a sparse-checkout of theories/, tools/, _process/ and the record-bound paths, so that history lookups work and blobs are fetched lazily. Alternatively, have scoped_drift distinguish 'history unavailable' from drift when the repository is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`).
issues.verify_reason: The finding holds. `.github/workflows/research.yml:9` uses `actions/checkout@v4` with no `fetch-depth`, so the clone is shallow. Since f6816a74e, `registry.validate` (tools/research/registry.py:491-498) sends every binding whose sha256 differs from the current file to `scoped_drift`. `reviewed_version` (:47-55) runs `git log HEAD -- path`; in a shallow clone that shows only the HEAD blob, and the per-user cache `~/.cache/research-source-versions.json` is absent on CI. `changed_lines` then returns None, and line 138-139 reports '(reviewed version not in history)'. Each such binding becomes reportable drift, and research.py exits 2. Locally, `python3 -B tools/research/research.py check` exits 0 with 0 errors and 0 source_drift, even though 248 bindings (all .md, in 158 records) differ from current bytes. Those all pass locally because the reviewed versions are found in full history. So the check is broken only where history is missing, and the content is not actually stale. Before f6816a74 the code also exited 2 on any drift, but landings re-hashed bindings then; since that commit they are deliberately left unrefreshed. Run history checks out: 57 failures since 2026-10-15T16:38Z (108e278e). Of these, 18 ran 6 steps and failed in 'Check records, evidence bindings…'. The other 39 have 0 steps and carry the annotation 'job was not started because recent account payments have failed' (checked on run 38787098534, 064c8add). The last success was 1a6c7c41 at 16:32Z. One wording fix: runs were still triggered up to 0cfb9c56 at 2026-10-16T13:22Z; the jobs just never started.
issues.corrected_fix: Restoring billing is Ren's call. The workflow fix is sound: `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0` (optionally `filter: blob:none`, since reviewed_version only needs old blobs for the 248 bound paths, which are fetched lazily). Better still, make scoped_drift report 'history unavailable' as an error that names the shallow clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`), so it cannot be mistaken for drift. Separately, consider a periodic re-binding pass so that 248 mismatches do not depend permanently on history lookups. Do this only after reading each change, as AGENTS.md requires, and never as blind re-hashing.

issues.title: 69 worktree checkouts use about 228 GB on a disk that is 91% full
issues.description: Each linked worktree is a full checkout of about 3.6 GB. There are 58 directories under .claude/worktrees (≈189 GB by du) and 11 more under /private/tmp and ~/.codex (≈39 GB). The volume shows 808Gi used and 82Gi free. All registered worktrees are merged into main or patch-equivalent: the three unmerged worktree-agent branches show '-' in `git cherry main`. All are clean except jolly-pike-140c94 and review-wt. Ten checkouts live in volatile /private/tmp. The 22 prunable admin entries (289 MB) belong to directories that are already gone. Move the four plain scratch dirs (p107-logs and the p116/117/119-tree .build caches) to an archive or the study dev dir. Do not run `git worktree prune` without Ren's explicit approval. For future landing and agent worktrees, use `git worktree add --no-checkout` plus a non-cone sparse-checkout profile (see the restructure list); this cuts each checkout to under 1 GB and shrinks the indexes.
issues.verify_reason: The figures reproduce. `du -sk .claude/worktrees` gives 189,341,104 KB across 58 directories. 54 of them are registered worktrees. The other 4 are plain directories: p107-logs (240 KB of bind-dry/bind-write logs), and p116-tree, p117-tree and p119-tree (~105 MB each). The last three are Lean source copies (Becoming/, Becoming.lean) plus .build, not just .build caches. There are 11 registered checkouts outside the repo: 10 under /private/tmp and 1 at ~/.codex/worktrees/meta-attractor-completion. Together they total 39,009,920 KB, so the overall figure is about 228 GB. `git worktree list` has 88 entries, 22 of them prunable. `df` reports 806Gi used, 84Gi free and 91% capacity. Every existing worktree is merged into main except the three worktree-agent branches (a450bc…, a61dac…, a75410…). For those, `git cherry main` shows only '-' lines, so they are patch-equivalent. All are clean except jolly-pike-140c94 (2 entries) and review-wt (2 entries). issues.corrected_fix: Make health-3 a hard precondition. Confirm ownership through ListAgents and the board, including land-p130, land-p129 and scoped-drift, which may belong to active sessions. issues.title: The object store holds about 1.9 GB of redundant packs and garbage; auto-gc loops on warnings
issues.description: pack-ff337bf0… (1.82 GB, 53,644 objects, 10-16 00:38) is entirely contained in pack-cb20b897… (1.85 GB). Across the 34 packs, 148,574 object entries cover only 89,626 distinct objects. There are 12 tmp_obj_* files totalling 344 MB from interrupted writes (seven of them, about 360 MB, were written 10-09 01:17–01:25 during the heald-2021 import), plus 5,285 loose objects. With gc.pruneExpire=never and no cruft packs, auto-gc cannot settle and records 'too many unreachable loose objects' in .git/gc.log. The unique object set is about 2.5 GB, against 4.4 GB used.
issues.evidence: `git count-objects -vH` (packs 34, size-pack 3.91 GiB, garbage 12, size-garbage 343.97 MiB); `git show-index < pack-ff337….idx` vs `< pack-cb20b….idx` with `comm -12` gives 53,644, equal to ff337's full count; `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch-check` sums blob disk to 2.47 GB; .git/gc.log dated 2026-10-15 21:13
issues.fix: Proposal only, with Ren's explicit go and no running sessions. (1) Make an APFS clone backup with `cp -c -R .git <backup>` and run `git fsck --connectivity-only`. (2) Move, do not delete, the tmp_obj_* files into an archive directory outside the repo with a sha256 manifest. (3) Set gc.reflogExpire=never, gc.reflogExpireUnreachable=never and gc.worktreePruneExpire=never, keeping gc.pruneExpire=never. (4) Run `git -c gc.cruftPacks=true gc` (git 2.39.5 supports cruft packs), which keeps every unreachable object in a cruft pack. Expected result: about 2.5 GB, with 0 objects lost. Run fsck again afterwards.
issues.verify_reason: The facts reproduce. `git count-objects -vH` reports 34 packs, size-pack 3.91 GiB, 5,285 loose objects (176.67 MiB), and garbage 12 at 343.97 MiB. All 53,644 objects of pack-ff337bf0 are in pack-cb20b897, which has 58,948. `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` gives 94,911 distinct objects: 89,626 in packs plus 5,285 loose. Their total on-disk size is 2.49 GB. .git/gc.log is dated 10-15 21:13 and reads 'too many unreachable loose objects', and gc.pruneexpire=never. Two details are off. First, six tmp_obj files (not seven) date from 10-09 01:17–01:25 and total ~360 MB; all 12 total 360,677,376 bytes (344 MiB). Second, pack-cb20b897 is from 10-16 20:07 and loose-6071….pack from 19:15, so repacking is happening today and the redundancy may be partly transient. On severity: about 1.9 GB is under 1% of the 228 GB worktree cost, and it affects neither results nor correctness, so minor rather than major.
issues.corrected_fix: The proposal is acceptable only with Ren's explicit go, with no sessions running (packs are being rewritten today), and after the worktree cleanup. Note that setting gc.reflogExpire, gc.reflogExpireUnreachable and gc.worktreePruneExpire changes persistent config, which is Ren's decision. gc.worktreePruneExpire=never is required before any `git gc`, because gc otherwise runs worktree prune. Move the tmp_obj files out with a sha256 manifest; do not delete them. Check with `git fsck --connectivity-only` before and after.

issues.description: There are 50,191 tracked files in 885 timestamped run folders, against 735 canonical theory, record, tool and root files. Of 70,494 tracked blobs, my scan of `git ls-tree -r -l HEAD` finds 48,285 files in 799 `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.ffffffZ/` folders (48,507 in 816 with a looser pattern), about 69% and 662 MB raw, against the finding's 50,191 in 885 and 71%. Its exact figures are not reproducible from the stated method, but the scale is right. 48,110 of those files are under experiments/integrated-correction. These counts match exactly: 12,647 empty blobs (12,366 inside run folders), becoming-checks with 31,786 files and 3,014 unique blobs, 98 distinct run paths cited by records, 104 of 171 becoming receipts without source_commit, 36,660 surplus duplicate copies of non-empty blobs, and the README:143 '2026-10-12 起' rule. The 104 pre-12-October runs have no source_commit, so their source copies are those receipts' own provenance and must stay addressable. registry.py reads only the receipt JSON (`read.receipt` and `read.elaborated` at :213-230), so keeping the *.json is enough for research-check, but not for provenance.

If Ren later approves thinning HEAD, move the run-folder bodies to an archive: a git tag or bundle such as `history/run-folders-<date>`, plus an in-repo manifest giving each moved path, sha256 and size, and a README pointer. Keep every receipt JSON, every record- or link-cited file, and the full source copies of the 104 runs without source_commit in place, or make them retrievable from the manifest by commit and path. Stopping the checker from writing zero-byte logs (record size and sha256 in the receipt instead) is fine for future runs. Do not rewrite past receipts.

areas.summary:
Scope: do the Chinese and English versions say the same thing? I checked the canonical chapter theories/becoming/chapters/THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md (962,442 B, 1,897 lines), all 229 records (theories/becoming/results/records/*.json), OPENING, GLOSSARY.md and the chapter's §10 glossary. Method: scripts in the scratchpad classified each line by language, aligned zh runs with the en runs that follow, and compared numbers, dates, Lean names, record ids and D/P ids. A keyword pass checked modal, quantifier and condition words. I then read at least 32 record statement pairs, the four open targets, and the flagged chapter pairs by hand.

Findings in short:
(1) Where the chapter is translated paragraph by paragraph, the two languages agree very closely. This holds for 'In one sentence', 'The theory stated in full' (22/22 paragraphs, en/zh byte ratio 1.13), §6.8–§6.12, §6.15 and 'Part I stated whole' (90/90 paragraphs, 0 Lean names in only one language). I found no quantifier, modality or ¬¬ drift there, apart from one dropped 'stepwise' (逐步).
(2) The real asymmetry is structural. Four apparatus pieces have Chinese-only content: the premise card, the §8 status table, the §9 module table and the §10 glossary meanings. §1–§5, §6.1–§6.7 and §7 have English that is a condensed summary, not a translation. As a result, 656 distinct Lean names, 144 of 162 record-link targets and 22 of 31 links to Ren's source words appear only on the Chinese side. English readers are sent to 'the glossary' for the ¬¬ rest-strength convention, and that explanation exists only in Chinese.
(3) There are substantive divergences in attribution and terminology:
- The two languages flip on who decided how 生生 is read (line 93 vs 126, and line 748 vs 757).
- The Chinese record metaethical-core-characterization and the glossary row map 生生 onto the Lean predicate `living`. The chapter's own premise card says the `living` readings exclude further generation, and decision D1 reads 生生 as the generative space. So the Chinese side names more than the Lean shows.
- 'unceasing generation' names the weak `Unceasing` predicate in the chapter but 生生不息 in GLOSSARY.md.
- 生成 carries three senses: becoming, formation and generative.
- 识 and 登记 are both rendered 'registration'.
(4) Records are structurally sound. All 229 have every zh/en leaf filled, and laws are paired item by item. After normalisation only one genuine numeric divergence remains: recurrence-without-premise says 40 modules where the Chinese and the receipt say 75.

Correction to the task brief: OPENING's source (sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-10-truth-exists-opening.md) is Ren's English, not a Chinese original. Ren himself asked on 10 October 2026 that no Chinese be left without English.

How this connects to the repo: the chapter is the canonical entry, and the records feed the generated views. These views (RESEARCH.md, LEAN-INDEX.md, the record .md pages) are bilingual line by line. The gaps sit in hand-written chapter apparatus and condensed English prose. Fix them by generating the apparatus from bilingual data and adding a parity check to make research-check, not by more hand edits.

proved.claim: Part I stated whole: the chapter's summary of what holds with no axiom is faithfully bilingual.
proved.conditions: Representation commitments (discrete steps, natural-number amounts, shared index), with decidability local to each law. Receipts: consolidated 20261015T231055.702986Z, plus today's fresh core run (_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/development/i5-checker-reproducible/REPORT.md).
proved.assessment: 90 zh paragraphs pair with 90 en. Number, Lean-name and modality checks found no divergence, except line 1281 dropping 逐步 ('stepwise') from 'balance is assumed only on registered conditions'. This is the most reliable bilingual statement of the theory.

proved.claim: Characterization of G0: on a connected whole with some living claim, G0 at every standpoint is equivalent to a seed S0 plus the two boundary neutralities N_rel and N_std.
proved.conditions: Valuation.Connected and one living claim; `living` is an abstract predicate (Metaethics.lean:130, 207).
proved.assessment: Mostly definitional. The Chinese at line 715 admits that the G0 ⇒ premises direction is almost trivial; the English (717) omits this. The Chinese record names the object 生生, but Lean proves it only for whatever `living` is supplied, and the supplied readings exclude further generation (premise card, line 141).

proved.claim: Rest theorem: a balanced, dissipative world with a census, embodied arising and enclosure from some step on cannot fail to come to rest.
proved.conditions: Counted, StandingCensus, ArisingEmbodied, Balanced, Dissipative, AroundStanding from T. The conclusion is ¬¬∃N, RestsFrom N, not ∃N.
proved.assessment: The record laws state 'cannot be refuted' / 不能被否证 in both languages, and OPENING's 'cannot go on forever without coming to rest' matches ¬¬. But the headlines in the chapter and in record statements say 'comes to rest' / 归于静止. The convention that this means the proved strength is written only in the Chinese glossary row (line 1793), which English line 110 points to.

proved.claim: With the one axiom (Unrestricted) as a condition, G0, S0 at every standpoint, both neutralities and a seed follow on every reading; the theory does not assert the axiom.
proved.conditions: Unrestricted is a hypothesis. The 22 theorems that use it are listed in PART-II-INVENTORY §3.1.
proved.assessment: Bilingual parity is good: both languages say 'conditional, not asserted'. Close to definitional, since the chapter itself says the axiom 'is G0 for anything'. Provenance links to Ren's words appear only in the Chinese paragraphs.

proved.claim: Decomposition of the axiom: Unrestricted is exactly each standpoint's presupposition on its closure, plus boundary invariance.
proved.conditions: Boundaries drawn along a relation, with the whole admissible; the general form also needs covering.
proved.assessment: Both languages agree and both say the decomposition 'locates the step, does not lower the axiom'. Substantive as a relocation, not a derivation.

proved.claim: In a finite family, coming to be and ceasing to be keep pace.
proved.conditions: The family is a finite List, with the instance [∀ a t, Decidable (p a t)] (Change.lean:481).
proved.assessment: The record statement says 'this needs no premise' in both languages. The decidability instance is mentioned in the chapter (item 2) and in OPENING's footnote, but not in the record statement. It is consistent across languages, but the condition is left out of the headline.

issues.title: Chinese equates 生生 with the Lean `living` predicate in the G0 record and the glossary
issues.description: The Chinese claim says the formal result shows '“每一生生从每一立场都有正面意义”（G0 在主张层的形式）' and uses 生生 seven times for the Lean `living` claims. The chapter glossary row maps 生生 → `living` (chapter line 1693), and the Chinese title of becoming-renewal-reading is '运行上的更新与生生的关系读法'. But the chapter's own premise card says the three `living` readings 'read activity compatible with others' dependence and do not include further generation, and whether that is 生生 is a philosophical argument' (line 141). §6.3 (757) and D1 also say 生生 is read as the generative space and that comparison uses no reading of `living`. So the Chinese claims the Lean characterizes G0 for 生生, while Lean proves it for an abstract `living` predicate (Metaethics.lean:207 `def G0 (F) (living : C → Prop)`). The English says 'every living claim'.
issues.evidence: jq -r .claim.zh theories/becoming/results/records/metaethical-core-characterization.json | head -c 300; chapter lines 141, 757, 1693; becoming-renewal-reading.json line 5; Metaethics.lean:207
issues.fix: Chinese claim: replace 生生 with 活的主张 / 活的内容, matching the English. Glossary row 1693: point the Lean column at the generative-space declarations (Web.paths / Widens, per §6.13) and add that `living` is the activity reading, not 生生. Change the Chinese title of becoming-renewal-reading to '…与活的关系读法'.
issues.verify_reason: The inconsistency is real. The Chinese claim of metaethical-core-characterization uses 生生 7 times where the English says 'living claim'. Glossary row 1693 maps 生生 → `living`. The Chinese title of becoming-renewal-reading reads '…生生的关系读法' while its English title is '…relational reading of living'. Both contradict D1 of DELEGATED-CHOICES, which says the readings of `living` 'stay as readings of what is counted, not as definitions of 生生'. They also contradict chapter lines 141 and 757. D1 itself lists both records as affected, yet neither was updated. Critical overstates it, though. G0 (Becoming.Metaethics `def G0 (F) (living : C → Prop) (positive)`, `∀ s c, living c → F.realized s c → positive s c`) takes `living` as a free parameter, so the characterization holds for any predicate on claims. The mathematics is not wrong; the Chinese wrongly identifies the parameter with 生生 and conflicts with a recorded decision. That is a stale canonical wording at major level, not an unsupported result. The repo already renders `living` claims as 活的主张 (held-lives-g0-is-centering.json uses it 16 times, axiom-decomposition also uses it), so the proposed wording matches practice. One part of the proposed fix is off: D1 names `Web.Widens` (and `Web.widens_iff_retains_adds`) as the formal reading of 生生, not 'Web.paths'.
issues.corrected_fix: In metaethical-core-characterization claim.zh (and any matching zh statement fields), replace 生生 with 活的主张 / 活的内容 where it renders `living`, matching the English. Change the zh title of becoming-renewal-reading to '运行上的更新与活的关系读法'. Keep the record ids and aliases, and run make research-render and research-check. In glossary row 1693, set the Lean column to `Web.Widens` (per D1), not `living`. Add a separate row for `living` as the reading of what is counted, linked to D1. Add a history note in each record citing D1.

English item 11 (line 126) says 'the readings of 生 and 生生 are Ren's'. The Chinese §6.3 paragraph (line 748) ends '哪一种读法或组合是生生的读法，是 Ren 方向内的规范与诠释选择，本章不替 Ren 作出' (that choice is Ren's to make and this chapter does not make it for him). issues.title: The English points to a Chinese-only explanation of what 'comes to rest' proves
issues.description: English line 110 says 'the world comes to rest… (`World.rests_unrefuted`; the strength proved is in the glossary)'. The glossary row (1793) gives the convention, 'when this chapter says a theorem comes to rest it means the strength it proves: from some step on rest cannot be refuted… finding that step needs LPO', in Chinese only. The English prose has 19 positive 'comes/brings to rest' headlines (e.g. 281, 1275, and the record space-and-its-parts statement 'dissipation brings a finite world to rest'). Lean proves `¬ ¬ ∃ N, w.RestsFrom N` (Openness.lean:614-618). Only the declaration suffix and the record laws give the ¬¬ strength in English.

issues.verify_reason: The convention is Chinese-only, as claimed. Glossary row 1793 explains, only in Chinese, that 'comes to rest' means the proved strength (¬¬∃N, named `unrefuted`), and English line 110 points to it. Lean confirms the strength: `comes_to_rest_unrefuted` in Openness.lean:614-618 concludes `¬ ¬ ∃ N, w.RestsFrom N`. The record space-and-its-parts says 'dissipation brings a finite world to rest' unqualified, but its Chinese is equally unqualified (归于静止), so that part is a strength-wording issue in both languages, not a parity gap. The claim that 'only the declaration suffix and record laws give the ¬¬ strength in English' is refuted. Line 110 itself says 'that arising stops cannot be refuted once every step…'. Line 572 says 'That it comes to rest is unrefuted, a double negation'. Lines 473, 959 and 1538 also state double-negation strength in English. The two readings are classically equivalent, so the risk is a constructive-strength nuance, not a false claim: minor.
issues.corrected_fix: Add an English sentence of the convention to glossary row 1793, e.g. 'when this chapter says a theorem brings a world to rest it means the strength proved: from some step on rest cannot be refuted (¬¬∃N; finding the step needs LPO)'. Optionally state it once in Part I English. Leave the headlines as they are, since the convention covers them. If the record statements are revised, qualify both zh and en together.

- Every declaration named in the three canonical statement sections resolves to a core declaration in the receipt, and each one is cited by at least one record. Scratch crosswalk: 643 rows.

areas.summary:
This area covers what in the tracked tree is sensitive, whether it has been pushed, and what fixing each item would take. Short answer: the GitHub remote yongxu/theories is PRIVATE (gh api: private=true, visibility=private, forks_count=0, has_pages=false, license=null, size 1,438,984 KB, pushed_at 2026-10-16T13:22:24Z). According to the local refs, main and origin/main are identical (0 commits ahead, 0 behind). The remote also holds 9 claude/* branches, all already merged into main. The 60 refs/codex/* checkpoint refs and 142 local branches look local-only (no push refspec is configured), but nobody has checked this with ls-remote. The repo tracks 70,495 files (about 3.59 GB in the working tree).

Every sensitive category below is on the remote. None of these files was ever deleted from history, and nearly all of them arrived with b8591afbf ("Track the full theories corpus", 2026-09-25). That commit is followed by 1,226 of the 1,229 commits on main, and it is reachable from all 11 remote refs. The friend recordings came in a6e63bdcf (2026-10-03) and the Guardian Anarchy and Soi Si Lom material in deabb7c2f (2026-10-04). Untracking a file therefore only stops future exposure. Getting bytes off the remote would mean rewriting the whole history, force-pushing every ref, and asking GitHub to purge caches. Existing clones would still hold copies: 88 worktrees, the cloud sessions behind origin/claude/*, and CI checkouts. A rewrite would also change every commit ID; about 362 distinct commit hashes are cited in theories/ and _process/ documents, plus more in Ren's memory files.

What I found:
- One live-format OpenRouter API key appears 5 times in 4 files (sources/14 and _process/reading-notes/cb-03.md). This is the only credential pattern anywhere in HEAD or history.
- Third-party personal data:
  - a named third party's illness, across 7 claude.ai chats plus derived notes;
  - ASR transcripts of conversations with friends, including a friend_name field in the metadata. No consent record exists.
- Field notes written by someone else sit in sources/00.
- Ren's own sensitive data:
  - chats on mental health, intimate life and admin/visa topics, and memory summaries that record location, job, health and relationships. These came in through an automatic length/keyword selection (sources/SOURCES.md:440), with no inclusion policy;
  - _ALL-719-INDEX.tsv, which lists all 718 chat titles, including chats that were not selected;
  - his personal email in 19 files and mail-server infrastructure details;
  - a corporate-domain (google.com) author email on 1,021 commits, set in the global ~/.gitconfig;
  - street-level Voice Memos location labels in folder and file names.
- About 35 third-party PDFs have no license record, plus full-text extractions of Kuhn and Popper. There is no repo LICENSE.
- Guardian Anarchy material was pushed even though Ren said 「不要发布它，我要的是本地版本」: a 9.6 MB site tarball containing a hosting manifest, plus about 16 MB of images.
- The experiments/guardian-anarchy gitlink has no .gitmodules. On GitHub it is a dangling pointer; locally it is a single uncopied 40 MB nested repo.

The irreplaceable originals that are deliberately local-only (about 205 MB or more of audio, and the nested repo) would be destroyed by `git clean -X` or lost in a fresh clone. Any restructure must protect them.

In HEAD, put a labelled redacted reading edition in place of the 5 occurrences, replacing the key with <redacted-openrouter-key>.
