issues.description: Every sensitive item has been present, never deleted, since b8591afbf (followed by 1,226 of 1,229 commits) or since a6e63bdcf/deabb7c2f (2026-10-03/04), and is reachable from all 11 remote refs, 142 local heads, 60 refs/codex and 88 worktrees. The recommendation is sound: no rewrite, revoke the key, and if publication ever happens, build a curated, history-free edition from an allow-list. It also fits the repo's rules on keeping cited hashes and never pruning.
issues.corrected_fix: Fold this into privacy-1 as its rationale rather than keeping it as a separate finding. Keep the history intact, and never run gc or prune. A future public edition is a new repo built from an allow-list tree.

areas.summary:
Scope: what the eight proposed move sets (A-H) would break, measured once with a single method across the whole repository (HEAD 0cfb9c56; 70,495 tracked files; 68,763 text files scanned, 2 files over 30 MB skipped). Method: (md) Markdown inline links, reference definitions and href/src targets, resolved relative to the referring file (absolute /Users/ren/theories/ and GitHub blob/main forms are accepted too); (raw) every path-like token in any text file, resolved relative to the referrer, then to the repo root (for tokens containing '/'), then, for referrers under lean/, relative to the Lean root and lean/becoming. raw includes md. A hit is a member file, or a directory whose tracked files all belong to the set. Referrers are grouped as nav/canonical, live process, records+goals, catalogue/config, generated, evidence, sources, python, other live, and intra-set. Scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/049c56d9-3ef4-495e-89fe-03128c9551ed/scratchpad/review/restructure-impact/ (sets.json, hits.json, matrix.txt, refined_sets.json, F_free_runs.json). The earlier reviewer estimates differ because they mixed these bases. Under this one method the totals are: A 4,553 raw / 2,673 md in 1,086 files; B 23,750 / 9,305 in 973; C 1,591 / 485; D 4,743 / 1,114; E 118 / 31; F 64,412 / 700; G 2,392 / 273; H 61,171 / 31,694 in 2,368 files.

Main findings:
- Most of the cost sits in registers and checkers, not in prose. Sha-pinned record references (2,870), proof bindings (1,059, all keyed by module name, so a move changes paths only), the reading catalogue (every chapters/*.md must have a row), Ren's curated generativity chain (1,222 links, 1,082 reviewed sources), goal sources, 92 freeze manifests that pin repo-root paths, and hard-coded tool paths.
- F is not 'superseded'. 247 of the 576 non-latest run folders are still cited: 854 proof-binding receipts in 209 records point into them, and 23 inherited modules have passed receipts only inside run folders. Moving those folders out of the Lean root would make check_becoming.py fail at L2129.
- G gains nothing. FOUNDATION modules are found by file stem, GenerativeCore.lean is freeze-pinned, and 113+ older checkers hard-code its path.
- H needs edits in 220 records (5,037 path strings), 247 hand-written links in THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md, 59 Lean-side checkers and lean_catalogue.group(). Defer it.
- What can move cleanly: 100 of the 131 A chapters (31 are tied to the canonical entry, goals or records); 1,643 of the 2,148 B packets; all 319 C_early files; 8 of the 9 studies (421 files); 11 of the 12 E files.
- Layout: use a directory named exactly 'history', placed per area at the same depth as the material it holds. That name matches check_becoming's ARCHIVE pattern, research.py working() and the 10-09 preservation list. It keeps 97% of outward links for single-set moves (A: 88 of 3,143 break), whereas a single mirrored top-level root breaks them all and would take receipts out of the Lean root. Cross-set links between moved sets still break (4,080 of about 18,300 in the combined plan), so Ren must choose between bytes-preserved-plus-path-map and the 10-09 links-only transform with carried hashes.
- Tooling: the 10-09 tooling cannot be reused as is. check_rename.py hard-codes its receipt name, checks only moves[0][0], knows only directory-prefix rules and four pin kinds, and verifies at its own add-commit. Generalize it in a new checker and leave the original in place (it still passes today).

Of the 576 non-latest run folders, 247 (13,633 files) are still cited: 56 by record references and proof bindings (854 proof-binding receipts in 209 records), 200 by the current core receipt's inherited_receipts, and 59 by generated views. The core receipt lists 78 inherited modules, and every one has at least one cited receipt in a latest run folder, which is outside F (F is the 576 non-latest runs out of 768 runs in 192 run dirs). issues.title: The choice of history layout decides how many links break; a mirrored top-level root is the worst option
issues.description:
Outbound Markdown links from moved files were tested under two layouts, keeping file bytes unchanged.
- Same-depth per-area 'history' sibling, one set at a time: A loses 88 of 3,143 outward links, B 206 of 6,264, D 51 of 775.
- Mirrored top-level history/<original path>: every outward link breaks (A 3,143, B 6,264, D 775).
- Combined plan (A_quiet to theories/becoming/history, B+C_early to <study>/history, D to _process/history): 4,080 of 18,298 resolvable links break under siblings, against 6,212 under a mirrored root, because the cross-set geometry changes.
A top-level root also takes Lean receipts out of the Lean root (see issue 2). It would also leave any .lean file there with path_role None, so the catalogue would list it as a working source.
issues.evidence: <scratchpad>/review/restructure-impact/outbound.py, design.py and design_m.py (read-only). Already-broken links inside the sets: C_early 9,849, D 1,730, B 120.
issues.fix: Use one directory name, 'history', placed per area at the same depth: theories/becoming/history/, _process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/history/ (mirroring root-foundation's internal layout), _process/history/<study>/ and _process/history/ for the September files. Ren then picks one policy: (a) keep bytes and publish a TSV path map (the 10-09 evidence policy), or (b) apply a one-time links-only transform to moved files and carry their pinned hashes, verified by re-derivation (the 10-09 method).
issues.verify_reason: Running outbound.py reproduces the outward-link numbers exactly. Same-depth sibling: A 88/3,143, B 206/6,264, D 51/775. Mirrored root: all outward links break. Three caveats. (1) The comparison holds only under keep-bytes. Under policy (b), which rewrites links in moved files, layout matters little. (2) Inbound links from unmoved files break the same way under either layout, and those are the larger count (e.g. B->A 1,560 and C->B 2,068 raw). (3) The repo already has a history mechanism the proposal does not mention: _process/architecture/history/<sha16>/ stores raw bytes plus a labelled .reading.md edition with adapted links. history-manifest.json indexes it ('Exact pre-reorganization bytes plus separately labelled local-link-adapted reading editions'), and navigation.py L19 reads it. That is exactly what AGENTS.md asks of portable reading editions. Also, the tested B sibling was root-foundation-history, not the proposed '<study>/history'. The depth is the same, so the numbers carry over.
issues.corrected_fix: Choose the policy first, then the layout. With keep-bytes, use same-depth 'history' siblings as proposed. With links adapted, follow the existing history-manifest pattern: keep the exact bytes as provenance, and register any adapted file as a labelled reading edition with its own sha256. Do not build a second, parallel convention. Either way, publish a TSV old-to-new path map and count inbound breakage separately.

issues.title: The 10-09 rename tooling cannot be reused as is
issues.description:
check_rename.py has these limits:
- It hard-codes its receipt name (L20).

areas.summary:
Scope covered: every empirical number and verdict in the 4 public-data assessment records, the three recipient chapters, EMPIRICAL-SCOPE, COST-SENSITIVE-LEARNING, TOOL-EVIDENCE-AND-AUTHORITY, MEMORY-CORRECTION-AND-SUCCESSION, MEASURED-FEEDBACK-CORRESPONDENCE and the empirical section of THE-THEORY-OF-EVOLUTION, plus all freeze manifests and source manifests. The canonical chapter THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md and theories/becoming/OPENING.md cite no repository empirical numbers. OPENING labels its empirical claims as the author's judgment or cites literature ([^present], [^transitions]).

Numbers. About 230 cited figures were checked against committed outputs and none mismatched. Six analyses were recomputed from raw data with independent scripts kept in the scratchpad: the cue paired statistics (the bootstrap reproduced exactly, including the mean_sequence sha256), the harm contrast (−841/5040), the reward primary and cell table from data_clean/data_3.csv, AgentDojo label counts from the 320 trajectories, the evolution focal-assay sums (42/72 vs 7/72), and the memory-updating figures. Source integrity also holds. All sha256s in the empirical source manifests match the tracked bytes, including the 18 Heald files and 398 reward files. The four harm originals also match OSF's upstream hashes.

Honesty. The scope wording is generally careful. Every reanalysis is labelled retrospective or exploratory, not preregistered. Known prior information is disclosed, and so are adverse and uncertain results. Synthetic studies (situated-discovery, evaluator-succession, learned-claim-agents) are labelled synthetic and are not cited as empirical support in theories/.

Weaknesses:
1. Freeze integrity. The 10-09 rename commit 87fdbb077d rewrote links inside frozen protocols (cue, selective-handoff, agentdojo correction-action and others). Some frozen states were never committed at all. Separately, "frozen before calculation" is self-attested: for every retrospective reanalysis, freeze and results were first committed in the same commit. The one exception is learned-claim-agents.
2. Navigation. There is no current evidence index. EMPIRICAL-SCOPE (10-06) predates most public-data work. Only 4 of 229 records are empirical. The canonical §8 links no evidence. Unrun discriminating protocols appear in no open record. Ren's 10-08 directive "Pursue full experimental validation" is missing from the directive register.
3. Two correspondences are described in confirmation language. The six-study literature synthesis is called "direct experimental support", and the M20 row of GENERATIVITY-CHAIN repeats this. The TCLab replay is presented as "physical correspondence ... established", although it is a log-versus-code consistency check.

Restructuring centres on four steps:
- a generated EVIDENCE index built from new assessment records;
- an open record listing the unrun discriminators;
- freeze reconciliation receipts plus a freeze checker;
- a typed (empirical, AI-run, synthetic, formal) generated experiments index in place of the status-paragraph experiments/README.md.

Nothing needs deleting.

issues.title: 10-09 rename broke the hashes of frozen empirical protocols

issues.verify_reason: The hash mismatches are real, and the rename commit 87fdbb077 caused every one listed. But 'No document or check records the breakage' is wrong. _process/architecture/rename-2026-10-09.json lists every rewritten file with sha256_before and sha256_after. For each affected file, sha256_before equals the frozen hash: cue PROTOCOL.md 44fe0ae4 -> 0ecb9622, selective-handoff PROTOCOL.md 7150bc30 -> c00a06f3. _process/architecture/check_rename.py re-derives each rewritten file from base commit 97930164 and checks the hashes. So the frozen bytes can be recovered, and the link-only nature of each change is checked by a tool. What is actually missing: no freeze JSON or experiment README points to that manifest. The sentence in selective-handoff/README.md:44 ('preserved under its frozen hash') is now accurate only through git history. And the rename's preservation rule protected frozen/ and development* directories but not freeze-bound files at their live paths. Severity is minor because provenance is intact and checker-verified. Separately, reason-replay PROTOCOL.md (fa819fe0f) and formation/formal/FormedSelection.lean (74cba5b13, bound by the succession protocol-freeze.json) diverged for other reasons.

issues.title: Compatible published exemplars presented as 'direct empirical support'
issues.description: Row M20 says 'situated learning, revision and useful recovery have direct empirical support, completing the targeted operational evidence synthesis'. The six studies (including Bongard 2006 robots) were selected after Ren's 10-08 remark '我觉得文献中应该已经有大量实验支撑，可以让你搞定' ('I think the literature should already have plenty of experimental support, enough for you to get it done'). issues.verify_reason: The compression in the chain is real. GENERATIVITY-CHAIN.md:101 (M20) says 'situated learning, revision and useful recovery have direct empirical support, completing the targeted operational evidence synthesis' with no qualifier. The source note was written right after Ren's '我觉得文献中应该已经有大量实验支撑，可以让你搞定' ('I think the literature should already have plenty of experimental support, enough for you to get it done'), so there is a confirmation-selection risk. However, the source note itself carries the qualifiers the reviewer says are missing. Line 7: 'targeted synthesis, not an exhaustive systematic review... or claim that the papers endorse our whole theory'. Line 11: the experiments 'do not uniquely establish this ontology'. Line 63: 'They support a mechanism class; they do not establish that all realizations obey'. Line 79 is a counterreview on cherry-picking. Read literally, the claim is that these operational phenomena are experimentally instantiated, which is true but weak. It is not a claim of support over rivals. So the problem lies in the curated chain row and the source note's bold zh line (AI-authored), not in the analysis. Minor wording.

So propose the change to Ren rather than applying it, through GENERATIVITY-CHAIN-INDEX-RECORD.md. areas.summary:
Scope: quote fidelity and decision provenance in the canonical layer. Checked: the Becoming chapter, OPENING, README, GOALS, AGENTS, the work board, the directive register and the 229 record JSONs. These were matched against sources/15-codex-theory-conversations (277 files plus one attachment dir), sources/16-claude-code-directions (15 files), and, read-only, Ren's local Claude Code and Codex transcripts (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions).

Overall the canonical layer is careful. Results:
- 953 passages were tightly attributed to Ren (a quote right after "Ren wrote/said/chose/:" etc.). About 206 distinct Ren quotes match a directive record word for word or after whitespace, punctuation or case normalization. 100 occurrences have their source linked in the same paragraph or field; 447 are verbatim but unlinked there, mostly record history entries and 47 chapter quotes.
- Only 2 translations are presented as Ren quotes (register line 53, chapter line 578). One elision joins two separate messages (board line 36). 4 quotes link the wrong source.
- The source layer is faithful from 10-09 on: 66 of 69 records with Ren blockquotes match the local transcripts in full, and the other 3 are AI text the records themselves mark. Earlier Codex-era records (10-04 to 10-08) cannot be checked locally.

Real gaps are in provenance and status, not in wording:
1. About 10 governing Ren messages have no source record anywhere in sources/. Ren's messages on 10-14 (Bangkok time): "go with your recommendations … please finish your plan" and "please, do all". On 10-15: "dag order", "offer it to them, keep proving". On 10-16: "let's finish both", "do a full review … fix all". On 10-10: "not doing the paper anymore". They are quoted in 109 records and on the board, and exist only in transcripts, AI plans and session memory.
2. The directive register omits 19 directive records dated 10-09 to 10-16. Among them is Ren's 10-15 "if my earlier words are unreasonable, please keep note, not follow blindly". 51 directive records are linked from no index at all.
3. Reading status disagrees across layers:
   - Chapter section 8 ("What stays Ren's") omits the readings still marked "AI's, pending Ren" for P120, P123, P125, P126, P127 and P130.
   - The board's claims table still shows P118–P127 as "verified in scratch" or "claimed", and says P118's readings are pending, although the landing log and the records say they landed and Ren took them.
   - Stale "await Ren" markers remain at chapter line 517 and board line 152.
4. Several decisions are inferred from general assent but stated as fact: "Ren adopted counting the rest as a relatum" in six chapter places, from "please, finish all"; the three I4b readings "which Ren took", from "agree with other readings". This is a reserved representation decision.
5. Folder semantics. sources/15 holds about 14 AI research write-ups (the 10-04 and 10-05 research cycles, about 220 KB, with no Ren blockquotes) inside the folder treated as Ren's directive record. Six "Ren's own words" headings sit over sections whose own preambles say they are almost entirely AI-drafted.
6. OPENING. Its header says version 5 although version 6 was applied. Only 2 of its 83 main-text sentences are at least 90% a verbatim run of Ren's words, so "by Ren, edited with AI" understates the rewrite (Ren approved each version).

Process note: two of my scratch JSON outputs were briefly written into the repo root by a relative path. They were moved to the scratchpad straight away, and git status is clean.
